objects.description: Alias macro mapping dng_timespec to the C library timespec on Windows path. Note: this is a macro alias, not a typedef; included here for clarity though construction is via standard timespec.

Holds metadata and offsets for a single DNG camera profile embedded in a file, including matrices, hue/sat maps, tone curve, and identification strings. Provides parsing helpers from a dng_stream. Construction/destruction appear trivial; lifetime managed by owners that store it by value or in vectors.

Aggregates shared DNG metadata discovered while parsing TIFF/EXIF structures, including offsets, profiles, matrices, digests, and various calibration/ICC fields. Provides virtual parsing hooks from a dng_stream/exif context and post-parse validation. Constructed default; destruction virtual. Ownership: typically embedded in higher-level DNG processing objects (not shown here).

Represents a 1-dimensional tone curve. Internally stores control coordinates in fCoord as a vector of real-valued points (likely x,y pairs). Provides methods to set the curve to null/invalid states, validate, compare, and to solve/evaluate the spline representation via an external dng_spline_solver. Construction/destruction details are not specified here; default constructor is declared. Ownership semantics are not explicit; fCoord is a public member storing points.
Enumeration controlling how image buffer rows are padded when computing buffer sizes: no padding or padding to 16-byte multiples per scanline.

RAII profiling helper. On construction records a start time and on destruction reports elapsed time with the provided message. Copying is disabled. Uses TickTimeInSeconds/TickCountInSeconds internally (implementation not shown).

Singleton providing access to a precomputed 16-bit noise/dither buffer for randomized dithering. Non-copyable; constructed privately and accessed via Get(). Stores noise in an internal dng_memory_data.

Represents an XMP (Extensible Metadata Platform) manager for DNG SDK. Provides parsing, serialization, querying, and synchronization of XMP metadata with EXIF/IPTC/DNG structures. Manages an internal XMP SDK instance and offers utilities for GPS, arrays, structured properties, and orientation/image info sync. Details about memory ownership and certain collaborators depend on other SDK headers.

High-level wrapper around Adobe XMP metadata for DNG. Manages an internal implementation (dng_xmp_private) and provides parsing, querying, editing, serialization, and packaging to/from JPEG. Users must call InitializeSDK before use and TerminateSDK when done. Copy-constructible; assignment is private/disabled. Thread-safety and lifetime rules are not documented here.

functions.name: dng_show_message
functions.description: Displays a platform-specific assertion/message dialog or log entry in debug builds. Intended for reporting assertion failures or diagnostic messages during development. Only declared/available when qDNGDebug is enabled at compile time.
requirements: Only call when compiled with qDNGDebug enabled; the function is not declared in non-debug builds.
Parameter s must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer; passing NULL or an invalid pointer is undefined.
Side effects and threading behavior are unspecified; do not assume thread safety.
This function performs I/O (message display/logging); do not call from signal/async-unsafe contexts.

functions.name: dng_show_message_f
functions.description: Displays a formatted diagnostic/assertion message in debug builds, using printf-style formatting. Intended for reporting assertion failures or other debug-only diagnostics. Only declared/available when qDNGDebug is enabled at compile time.
requirements: Only call when compiled with qDNGDebug enabled; the function is not declared in non-debug builds.
Parameter fmt must be a valid, null-terminated C format string; must not be NULL.
The variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt (printf-style); mismatches cause undefined behavior.
Side effects and threading behavior are unspecified; do not assume thread safety.
This function performs I/O (message display/logging); do not call from signal/async-unsafe contexts.

functions.name: DNG_ASSERT
functions.signature: void DNG_ASSERT(bool condition, const char *msg);  // macro-like usage; implemented as a macro
functions.description: Debug assertion macro. In debug builds (qDNGDebug), if condition is false it displays msg via dng_show_message; in non-debug builds it compiles to a no-op. Use to document and check invariants during development without runtime cost in release builds.
requirements: This is a macro, not a function; arguments may be evaluated by the macro expansion. In debug builds, condition is evaluated once to decide the if-statement; in release builds it is not evaluated. Ensure condition has no required side effects.
Parameter msg should be a valid, null-terminated C string; do not pass NULL.
Do not rely on DNG_ASSERT being executed in non-debug builds; it expands to an empty do-while loop there.
If displaying msg has platform/UI side effects, avoid calling from signal/async-unsafe contexts.

functions.name: DNG_REQUIRE
functions.signature: void DNG_REQUIRE(bool condition, const char *msg);  // macro-like usage; implemented as a macro
functions.description: Requirement-checking macro that enforces preconditions. If condition is false it throws a program error via ThrowProgramError(msg). In debug builds (qDNGDebug), it also reports the failure via DNG_ASSERT before throwing. Use when failure must abort/throw in all builds.
requirements: This is a macro, not a function; in debug builds, condition may be evaluated more than once (once for the outer check and again inside DNG_ASSERT). Ensure condition has no side effects or is safe to evaluate multiple times when false.
Parameter msg must be a valid, null-terminated C string suitable for error reporting; do not pass NULL.
Callers must be prepared to handle the exception thrown by ThrowProgramError(msg) when condition is false.
Behavior depends on qDNGDebug: in debug builds a message is shown before throwing; in non-debug builds it directly throws.
Do not rely on any return value; this macro does not return if condition is false (it throws).

functions.name: DNG_REPORT
functions.signature: void DNG_REPORT(const char *msg);  // macro-like usage; implemented as a macro
functions.description: Informational report macro that routes msg to the debug assertion reporting mechanism. It expands to DNG_ASSERT(false, msg), forcing display/logging of msg in debug builds and becoming a no-op in non-debug builds. Useful for unconditional debug-only messages.
requirements: This is a macro, not a function; msg is passed to DNG_ASSERT.
Parameter msg must be a valid, null-terminated C string; do not pass NULL.
Effective only in debug builds (qDNGDebug); in non-debug builds it compiles to a no-op and performs no action.
Avoid use in contexts requiring async-signal safety; message display/logging may not be safe there.

functions.name: AutoPtr::AutoPtr
functions.description: Default-constructs an AutoPtr that owns no object (internal pointer set to null). Intended for stack scope RAII of a single object allocated with new.
requirements: Constructs an empty smart pointer; no managed object is owned initially.
Subsequent operations that dereference (operator->, operator*) require the pointer to be non-null.

functions.name: AutoPtr::~AutoPtr
functions.description: Destructor. Deletes the owned object (if any) using delete and clears the internal pointer.
requirements: The owned pointer, if non-null, must point to a single object allocated with operator new (not an array), as delete p_ is used.
No double-ownership: ensure no other owner deletes the same pointer.

functions.name: AutoPtr::Alloc
functions.description: Allocates a new T using T's default constructor and resets ownership to that new object, deleting any previously owned object.
requirements: T must be default-constructible (new T must be valid).
If an object is already owned, it will be deleted via delete before taking ownership of the new object.
Allocation failures will propagate as exceptions from operator new (e.g., std::bad_alloc).

functions.name: AutoPtr::Get
functions.description: Returns the raw pointer currently owned, or null if none. Does not transfer ownership and has no side effects.
requirements: Returned pointer, if non-null, remains owned by the AutoPtr; the caller must not delete it unless ownership is later released via Release().
Pointer may become invalid if the AutoPtr is destroyed or Reset afterward.

functions.name: AutoPtr::Release
functions.description: Releases ownership of the managed pointer and returns it to the caller. The AutoPtr becomes empty (null) and will not delete the object.
requirements: After Release, the caller becomes responsible for eventually deleting the returned pointer with delete (matching the allocation form).
Safe to call when no object is owned; returns null in that case.

functions.name: AutoPtr::Reset
functions.description: Replaces the managed pointer with p, deleting the previously owned object (if different and non-null). Takes ownership of p.
requirements: p must be either null or a pointer to a single T allocated with operator new (not new[]), since deletion uses delete.
If p equals the currently owned pointer, no deletion occurs.
After Reset, the caller must not delete p; ownership transferred to AutoPtr.

functions.name: AutoPtr::operator->
functions.description: Provides pointer-like access to the managed object members.
requirements: The AutoPtr must currently own a non-null pointer; calling operator-> on a null AutoPtr is an error and leads to undefined behavior.

functions.name: AutoPtr::operator*
functions.description: Dereferences the managed pointer to access the referenced object.
requirements: The AutoPtr must currently own a non-null pointer; calling operator* on a null AutoPtr is an error and leads to undefined behavior.

functions.name: Swap
functions.description: Swaps the owned pointers between two AutoPtr<T> instances without copying or deleting the managed objects.
requirements: x and y must be AutoPtr instances of the same template type T.
After swap, ownership is exchanged; callers must account for changed ownership.

functions.name: AutoArray::AutoArray
functions.description: Default-constructs an AutoArray that refers to a null pointer (no storage allocated).
requirements: No storage is allocated; Get() will return nullptr until Reset(count) or size-constructing constructor is used.
Dereferencing via operator[] is invalid until storage is allocated and within range.

functions.name: AutoArray::AutoArray
functions.description: Constructs an AutoArray with 'count' default-constructed elements. Manages lifetime automatically; memory is freed on scope exit.
requirements: T must be default-constructible.
count must fit in memory; on out-of-memory, a dng_exception with error code dng_error_memory is thrown (as documented).
Access via operator[] must be within [0, count).

functions.name: AutoArray::Reset
functions.description: Replaces the contents with a new array of 'count' default-constructed elements, destroying any previously held elements.
requirements: T must be default-constructible.
count must be non-negative (size_t) and reasonable; on out-of-memory, a dng_exception with error code dng_error_memory is thrown.
Any previously obtained raw pointer from Get() becomes invalid after Reset.

functions.name: AutoArray::operator[]
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the i-th element of the array.
requirements: Array storage must have been allocated via constructor or Reset before use.
i must be non-negative and less than the current size; accessing out of range is an error/undefined behavior.

functions.name: AutoArray::operator[]
functions.signature: template<typename T> const T &AutoArray<T>::operator[](ptrdiff_t i) const;
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the i-th element of the array.
requirements: Array storage must have been allocated via constructor or Reset before use.
i must be non-negative and less than the current size; accessing out of range is an error/undefined behavior.

functions.name: AutoArray::Get
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the first element of the array, or nullptr if no storage is allocated.
requirements: Do not dereference the returned pointer if it is null.
The returned pointer may be invalidated by subsequent Reset calls or destruction of the AutoArray.

functions.name: AutoArray::Get
functions.description: Returns a const pointer to the first element of the array, or nullptr if no storage is allocated.
requirements: Do not dereference the returned pointer if it is null.
The returned pointer may be invalidated by subsequent Reset calls or destruction of the AutoArray.

functions.name: SafeInt32Add
functions.signature: bool SafeInt32Add(std::int32_t arg1, std::int32_t arg2, std::int32_t *result)
functions.description: Checks whether arg1 + arg2 fits in a 32-bit signed integer without underflow/overflow. On success, writes the sum to *result and returns true; otherwise returns false and leaves *result unchanged. Use this when you need a non-throwing, checked add.
requirements: result must be a non-null pointer to writable std::int32_t storage
Caller must check the boolean return; if false, *result is unchanged
arg1 and arg2 may be any 32-bit signed values

functions.name: SafeInt64Add
functions.description: Returns arg1 + arg2 if the sum fits in int64_t; otherwise throws a dng_exception (dng_error_unknown).
requirements: On overflow or underflow, function throws dng_exception with error code dng_error_unknown
arg1 and arg2 may be any 64-bit signed values

functions.name: SafeUint32Add
functions.signature: bool SafeUint32Add(std::uint32_t arg1, std::uint32_t arg2, std::uint32_t *result)
functions.description: Checks whether arg1 + arg2 fits in uint32_t without wraparound. On success, writes the sum to *result and returns true; otherwise returns false and leaves *result unchanged.
requirements: result must be a non-null pointer to writable std::uint32_t storage
Caller must check the boolean return; if false, *result is unchanged
arg1 and arg2 may be any 32-bit unsigned values

functions.name: SafeUint64Add
functions.description: Returns arg1 + arg2 if the sum fits in uint64_t without wraparound; otherwise throws a dng_exception (dng_error_unknown).
requirements: On wraparound, function throws dng_exception with error code dng_error_unknown
arg1 and arg2 may be any 64-bit unsigned values

functions.name: SafeInt32Sub
functions.signature: bool SafeInt32Sub(std::int32_t arg1, std::int32_t arg2, std::int32_t *result)
functions.description: Checks whether arg1 - arg2 fits in int32_t without underflow/overflow. On success, writes the difference to *result and returns true; otherwise returns false and leaves *result unchanged.
requirements: result must be a non-null pointer to writable std::int32_t storage
Caller must check the boolean return; if false, *result is unchanged
arg1 and arg2 may be any 32-bit signed values

functions.name: SafeUint32Sub
functions.description: Returns arg1 - arg2 if the subtraction does not wrap around in uint32_t; otherwise throws a dng_exception (dng_error_unknown).
requirements: On wraparound, function throws dng_exception with error code dng_error_unknown
arg1 and arg2 may be any 32-bit unsigned values

functions.name: SafeInt32Mult
functions.description: Returns arg1 * arg2 if the product fits in int32_t without overflow; otherwise throws a dng_exception (dng_error_unknown).
requirements: On overflow, function throws dng_exception with error code dng_error_unknown
arg1 and arg2 may be any 32-bit signed values

functions.name: SafeUint32Mult
functions.signature: bool SafeUint32Mult(std::uint32_t arg1, std::uint32_t arg2, std::uint32_t *result)
functions.description: Checks whether arg1 * arg2 fits in uint32_t without wraparound. On success, writes the product to *result and returns true; otherwise returns false and leaves *result unchanged.
requirements: result must be a non-null pointer to writable std::uint32_t storage
Caller must check the boolean return; if false, *result is unchanged
arg1 and arg2 may be any 32-bit unsigned values

functions.name: SafeSizetMult
functions.description: Returns arg1 * arg2 if the product fits in size_t without overflow; otherwise throws a dng_exception (dng_error_unknown).
requirements: On overflow, function throws dng_exception with error code dng_error_unknown
arg1 and arg2 may be any size_t values

functions.name: SafeInt64Mult
functions.signature: inline std::int64_t SafeInt64Mult(std::int64_t arg1, std::int64_t arg2)
functions.description: Returns arg1 * arg2 if the product fits in int64_t without overflow; otherwise throws a dng_exception (dng_error_unknown). Implemented with platform-specific checks and may abort internally after throwing.
requirements: On overflow, function throws dng_exception with error code dng_error_unknown
arg1 and arg2 may be any 64-bit signed values

functions.name: SafeUint32DivideUp
functions.description: Returns ceil(arg1 / arg2) in uint32_t. If arg2 is zero, throws a dng_exception (dng_error_unknown). Guaranteed safe against wraparound for all inputs.
requirements: arg2 must be non-zero to avoid exception
On arg2 == 0, function throws dng_exception with error code dng_error_unknown
arg1 and arg2 may be any 32-bit unsigned values

functions.name: RoundUpUint32ToMultiple
functions.signature: bool RoundUpUint32ToMultiple(std::uint32_t val, std::uint32_t multiple_of, std::uint32_t *result)
functions.description: Finds the smallest multiple of multiple_of that is >= val. If this value fits in uint32_t and multiple_of != 0, stores it in *result and returns true; otherwise returns false and leaves *result unchanged.
requirements: result must be a non-null pointer to writable std::uint32_t storage
multiple_of must be non-zero for success; if zero, function returns false and does not modify *result
Caller must check the boolean return; if false, *result is unchanged
val and multiple_of may be any 32-bit unsigned values

functions.name: ConvertUint32ToInt32
functions.description: Checks whether val fits in int32_t. On success, writes the converted value to *result and returns true; otherwise returns false and leaves *result unchanged.
requirements: result must be a non-null pointer to writable std::int32_t storage
Caller must check the boolean return; if false, *result is unchanged
val may be any 32-bit unsigned value

functions.name: ConvertUnsigned
functions.signature: template <class TSrc, class TDest> static void ConvertUnsigned(TSrc src, TDest *dest)
functions.description: Converts an unsigned integer of type TSrc to unsigned integer type TDest without truncation. If conversion would truncate (i.e., src is not representable in TDest), throws a dng_exception (dng_error_unknown). Designed to work whether TDest is narrower, equal, or wider than TSrc.
requirements: TSrc and TDest must be unsigned integer types (enforced by static_assert)
dest must be a non-null pointer to writable TDest storage
If conversion would truncate, function throws dng_exception with error code dng_error_unknown
src may be any value representable by TSrc

functions.name: ConvertDoubleToInt32
functions.description: Converts val to int32_t using truncation if the value is within int32_t range; otherwise throws a dng_exception (dng_error_unknown).
requirements: If val is outside the representable int32_t range or not convertible via truncation, function throws dng_exception with error code dng_error_unknown
val may be any finite or non-finite double

functions.name: ConvertDoubleToUint32
functions.description: Converts val to uint32_t using truncation if the value is within uint32_t range; otherwise throws a dng_exception (dng_error_unknown).
requirements: If val is outside the representable uint32_t range or not convertible via truncation, function throws dng_exception with error code dng_error_unknown
val may be any finite or non-finite double

functions.name: ConvertDoubleToFloat
functions.description: Converts val to float. Values outside [-FLT_MAX, FLT_MAX] saturate to -infinity or +infinity respectively; NaN is preserved as NaN. No exception is thrown.
requirements: No special requirements; val may be any double, including NaN and infinities

functions.name: dng_string::dng_string
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates an empty dng_string which internally stores text as UTF-8.
requirements: Object must be constructed before use; no additional requirements.

functions.name: dng_string::dng_string
functions.description: Copy constructor. Initializes this string with the UTF-8 contents of another dng_string.
requirements: Source object s must be a valid, initialized dng_string.

functions.name: dng_string::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment. Replaces this string’s contents with those of another dng_string.
requirements: Both this and s must be valid dng_string objects.

functions.name: dng_string::~dng_string
functions.description: Destructor. Releases any resources held by the string.
requirements: Object must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: dng_string::Get
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal UTF-8, NUL-terminated character buffer representing the string.
requirements: Returned pointer remains valid while the dng_string object is alive and unmodified.
Do not write through the returned const char*.

functions.name: dng_string::IsASCII
functions.description: Returns true if the string can be represented entirely in 7-bit ASCII; false otherwise.
requirements: None beyond a valid dng_string instance.

functions.name: dng_string::Set
functions.description: Sets the string from a NUL-terminated C string. Encoding handling is library-defined; see Set_UTF8, Set_ASCII, Set_UTF8_or_System for explicit control.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string.
Caller should ensure the encoding of s is appropriate for this generic setter; use specific setters if necessary.

functions.name: dng_string::Set_ASCII
functions.description: Sets the string from a NUL-terminated 7-bit ASCII C string, converting to internal UTF-8 storage.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated ASCII string.

functions.name: dng_string::Set_UTF8
functions.description: Sets the string from a NUL-terminated UTF-8 C string.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string.

functions.name: dng_string::Get_SystemEncoding
functions.description: Converts the string to the current system’s native character encoding, writing the NUL-terminated result into buffer and returning the byte count (implementation-defined).
requirements: buffer must be a valid dng_memory_data instance ready to receive data.
Caller should not assume a specific encoding; it is system-dependent.
Returned length semantics (with or without NUL) are not specified here; verify via implementation if needed.

functions.name: dng_string::Set_SystemEncoding
functions.description: Sets the string from a NUL-terminated C string in the system’s native encoding, converting to internal UTF-8.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string encoded in the system’s native encoding.

functions.name: dng_string::ValidSystemEncoding
functions.description: Returns true if the string can be represented in the system’s native encoding without loss or invalid sequences.
requirements: None beyond a valid dng_string instance.

functions.name: dng_string::Set_JIS_X208_1990
functions.description: Sets the string from a NUL-terminated C string encoded as JIS X 0208:1990 (per name; header says X208_1990) and converts it to internal UTF-8.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string in JIS X 0208:1990 encoding.

functions.name: dng_string::DecodeUTF8
functions.signature: static uint32 dng_string::DecodeUTF8(const char *&s, uint32 maxBytes = 6, bool *isValid = NULL)
functions.description: Decodes a single Unicode code point from a UTF-8 byte sequence at s, advancing s past the decoded sequence. Returns the code point as a 32-bit value; sets isValid (if non-null) to indicate validity. maxBytes bounds the maximum bytes to consider.
requirements: s must reference a valid readable buffer containing a UTF-8 sequence; it must be advanced-able.
maxBytes should be between 1 and 6 inclusive (default 6).
If isValid is non-null, it must point to writable memory.

functions.name: dng_string::IsUTF8
functions.description: Returns true if the NUL-terminated C string at s is valid UTF-8; false otherwise.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string buffer.

functions.name: dng_string::Set_UTF8_or_System
functions.description: Sets the string from a NUL-terminated C string, attempting UTF-8 first and falling back to the system encoding if not valid UTF-8.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: dng_string::Get_UTF16
functions.description: Converts the string to UTF-16 and writes a NUL-terminated UTF-16 sequence into buffer, returning a length in bytes or code units (implementation-defined).
requirements: buffer must be a valid dng_memory_data instance ready to receive UTF-16 data.
Endianness and exact length semantics are not specified here; verify via implementation if needed.

functions.name: dng_string::Set_UTF16
functions.description: Sets the string from a NUL-terminated UTF-16 string, converting to internal UTF-8.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated UTF-16 string.

functions.name: dng_string::Clear
functions.description: Clears the string to empty.
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_string::Truncate
functions.description: Truncates the string’s internal UTF-8 data to at most maxBytes bytes. Behavior regarding partial code points is implementation-defined.
requirements: maxBytes is a non-negative byte count; range limits are not specified here.

functions.name: dng_string::TrimTrailingBlanks
functions.description: Removes trailing blank characters (likely spaces/tabs) from the end of the string. Returns true if any characters were removed.
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_string::TrimLeadingBlanks
functions.description: Removes leading blank characters from the start of the string. Returns true if any characters were removed.
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_string::IsEmpty
functions.description: Returns true if the string is empty.
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_string::NotEmpty
functions.description: Convenience method returning true if the string is not empty (logical negation of IsEmpty).
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_string::Length
functions.description: Returns the length of the string in bytes of its internal UTF-8 representation (exact unit is inferred; header does not specify code points vs bytes).
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_string::operator==
functions.description: Returns true if this string compares equal to s (comparison semantics are implementation-defined; typically byte-wise UTF-8 equality).
requirements: s must be a valid dng_string.

functions.name: dng_string::operator!=
functions.description: Returns true if this string does not equal s (logical negation of operator==).
requirements: s must be a valid dng_string.

functions.name: dng_string::Matches
functions.signature: static bool dng_string::Matches(const char *t, const char *s, bool case_sensitive = false)
functions.description: Utility for comparing two NUL-terminated C strings with optional case sensitivity. Returns true if they match under the specified mode.
requirements: t must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string.
s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: dng_string::Matches
functions.signature: bool dng_string::Matches(const char *s, bool case_sensitive = false) const
functions.description: Compares this string to the given C string with optional case sensitivity. Returns true if they match under the specified mode.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: dng_string::StartsWith
functions.signature: bool dng_string::StartsWith(const char *s, bool case_sensitive = false) const
functions.description: Returns true if this string begins with the given prefix s under the specified case sensitivity.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string (the prefix).

functions.name: dng_string::EndsWith
functions.signature: bool dng_string::EndsWith(const char *s, bool case_sensitive = false) const
functions.description: Returns true if this string ends with the given suffix s under the specified case sensitivity.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string (the suffix).

functions.name: dng_string::Contains
functions.signature: bool dng_string::Contains(const char *s, bool case_sensitive = false, int32 *match_offset = NULL) const
functions.description: Searches for substring s in this string with optional case sensitivity. Returns true if found. If match_offset is non-null, it receives the starting index of the first match.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string (the substring to search).
If match_offset is non-null, it must point to writable memory.

functions.name: dng_string::Replace
functions.signature: bool dng_string::Replace(const char *old_string, const char *new_string, bool case_sensitive = true)
functions.description: Replaces occurrences of old_string with new_string, using the specified case sensitivity. Returns true if any replacement occurred.
requirements: old_string must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string.
new_string must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: dng_string::TrimLeading
functions.signature: bool dng_string::TrimLeading(const char *s, bool case_sensitive = false)
functions.description: If the string starts with the given prefix s (per case sensitivity), removes that prefix and returns true; otherwise returns false.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string (the prefix to trim).

functions.name: dng_string::Append
functions.description: Appends a NUL-terminated C string to the end of this string, converting to internal UTF-8 as needed.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string in an expected encoding (prefer UTF-8 or use specific setters).

functions.name: dng_string::SetUppercase
functions.description: Converts the string to uppercase. Exact locale/Unicode handling is unspecified here.
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_string::SetLowercase
functions.description: Converts the string to lowercase. Exact locale/Unicode handling is unspecified here.
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_string::SetLineEndings
functions.description: Normalizes all line endings in the string to the specified single character (e.g., '\n' or '\r').
requirements: ending should be a single character; commonly '\n' or '\r'.

functions.name: dng_string::SetLineEndingsToNewLines
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to normalize all line endings to newline '\n'.
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_string::SetLineEndingsToReturns
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to normalize all line endings to carriage return '\r'.
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_string::StripLowASCII
functions.description: Removes low ASCII control characters from the string (inferred from name).
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_string::ForceASCII
functions.description: Forces the string to ASCII (e.g., by removing or mapping non-ASCII characters; details unspecified).
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_string::Compare
functions.description: Three-way comparison with another dng_string. Returns value analogous to strcmp (negative, zero, positive) based on ordering; exact collation rules unspecified.
requirements: s must be a valid dng_string.

functions.name: dng_string::NormalizeAsCommaSeparatedNumbers
functions.description: Parses the string for numeric fields and normalizes them into a comma-separated format (per utility description).
requirements: Input should contain numbers that can be recognized; exact parsing rules are unspecified.

functions.name: dng_string_list::dng_string_list
functions.description: Default constructor for dng_string_list. Initializes an empty list of dng_string entries with zero count and no allocated storage.
requirements: The object must be constructed before any other member function is called.

functions.name: dng_string_list::~dng_string_list
functions.description: Destructor for dng_string_list. Releases any resources owned by the list and its internal storage.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.
Ensure no references to elements in the list are used after the list is destroyed.

functions.name: dng_string_list::Count
functions.description: Returns the current number of strings stored in the list.
requirements: The dng_string_list instance must be valid (constructed and not yet destroyed).

functions.name: dng_string_list::operator[]
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the string at the specified index.
requirements: index must be less than Count(); behavior is undefined otherwise.
The list must contain at least one element before accessing.
The returned reference becomes invalid if the list is cleared, destroyed, or reallocated in a way that moves elements.

functions.name: dng_string_list::Allocate
functions.description: Ensures the list has capacity for at least minSize elements. Does not specify whether Count() changes; typically used to preallocate storage before inserts. Exact behavior not documented in this header.
requirements: minSize is the minimum capacity to ensure; must fit within available memory.
The list instance must be valid (constructed and not destroyed).

functions.name: dng_string_list::Insert
functions.signature: void dng_string_list::Insert(uint32 index, const dng_string & s)
functions.description: Inserts the given string s at the specified index, shifting existing elements at and after index to the right. Exact out-of-range handling is not documented; inferred to require index within [0, Count()].
requirements: index should be between 0 and Count() inclusive; behavior is undefined otherwise.
The input string reference s must be valid for the duration of the call.
The list instance must be valid (constructed and not destroyed).

functions.name: dng_string_list::Append
functions.description: Appends the given string s to the end of the list. Equivalent to Insert(Count(), s).
requirements: The input string reference s must be valid for the duration of the call.
The list instance must be valid (constructed and not destroyed).

functions.name: dng_string_list::Contains
functions.description: Returns true if the list contains a string equal to s; false otherwise. Comparison criteria are not documented here; assumed to rely on dng_string equality semantics.
requirements: The input string reference s must be valid for the duration of the call.
The list instance must be valid (constructed and not destroyed).

functions.name: dng_string_list::Clear
functions.description: Removes all strings from the list, resetting the count to zero. Allocation/pointer invalidation details are not documented; expect existing references/iterators to become invalid.
requirements: Do not use previously obtained references to elements after calling Clear().
The list instance must be valid (constructed and not destroyed).

functions.name: dng_point::dng_point
functions.description: Default constructor for dng_point. Initializes v and h to 0. Use to create an origin (0,0) integer point.

functions.name: dng_point::dng_point
functions.description: Constructs a dng_point with integer coordinates v=vv and h=hh. Use when integer point coordinates are known.
requirements: >= vv must be representable in int32 (by type).
>= hh must be representable in int32 (by type).

functions.name: dng_point::operator==
functions.description: Compares two dng_point objects for equality of both coordinates (v and h). Returns true if both match exactly.
requirements: pt must refer to a valid dng_point instance.

functions.name: dng_point::operator!=
functions.description: Inequality comparison for dng_point; logical negation of operator==.
requirements: pt must refer to a valid dng_point instance.

functions.name: dng_point_real64::dng_point_real64
functions.description: Default constructor for dng_point_real64. Initializes v and h to 0.0.

functions.name: dng_point_real64::dng_point_real64
functions.description: Constructs a dng_point_real64 with floating-point coordinates v=vv and h=hh.
requirements: >= vv must be representable in real64 (by type).
>= hh must be representable in real64 (by type).

functions.name: dng_point_real64::dng_point_real64
functions.description: Converts an integer dng_point to a floating-point dng_point_real64 by casting both coordinates to real64.
requirements: pt must refer to a valid dng_point instance.

functions.name: dng_point_real64::operator==
functions.description: Compares two dng_point_real64 objects for exact equality of both coordinates (bitwise equality on the doubles via ==).
requirements: pt must refer to a valid dng_point_real64 instance.
Be aware that exact == on floating-point values can be sensitive to rounding; this is by design here.

functions.name: dng_point_real64::operator!=
functions.description: Inequality comparison for dng_point_real64; logical negation of operator==.
requirements: pt must refer to a valid dng_point_real64 instance.

functions.name: dng_point_real64::Round
functions.description: Rounds the floating-point coordinates to the nearest integers and returns them as a dng_point using Round_int32 for each component.
requirements: v and h must be within the representable range of int32 for Round_int32 to succeed (inferred from name and use).
Caller should be prepared for project-defined behavior if rounding overflows int32 (e.g., exception/assert depending on Round_int32 implementation; behavior not specified here).

functions.name: operator+
functions.description: Adds two integer points component-wise using SafeInt32Add and returns the sum.
requirements: a and b must refer to valid dng_point instances.
Caller should be prepared for project-defined overflow handling from SafeInt32Add if the sum exceeds int32 range (inferred from function name; exact behavior not specified).

functions.name: operator+
functions.description: Adds two floating-point points component-wise and returns the sum.
requirements: a and b must refer to valid dng_point_real64 instances.

functions.name: operator-
functions.description: Subtracts two integer points component-wise using SafeInt32Sub and returns the difference (a - b).
requirements: a and b must refer to valid dng_point instances.
Caller should be prepared for project-defined overflow/underflow handling from SafeInt32Sub if the result exceeds int32 range (inferred from function name; exact behavior not specified).

functions.name: operator-
functions.description: Subtracts two floating-point points component-wise and returns the difference (a - b).
requirements: a and b must refer to valid dng_point_real64 instances.

functions.name: DistanceSquared
functions.description: Returns the squared Euclidean distance between two floating-point points: (a.v - b.v)^2 + (a.h - b.h)^2. Useful to compare distances without a square root.
requirements: a and b must refer to valid dng_point_real64 instances.
Inputs that are NaN or infinity will propagate according to IEEE-754 rules (inferred from use of real64).

functions.name: Transpose
functions.description: Returns a new dng_point with v and h swapped.
requirements: a must refer to a valid dng_point instance.

functions.name: Transpose
functions.description: Returns a new dng_point_real64 with v and h swapped.
requirements: a must refer to a valid dng_point_real64 instance.

functions.name: dng_rect::operator==
functions.description: Compares two dng_rect instances for equality. Although the body is not shown, equality for rectangle types typically means all four edges (t, l, b, r) are equal.
requirements: Input rectangle reference must be a valid dng_rect object.
No side effects; does not modify either rectangle.
Behavior details beyond field-wise equality are not documented; equality of all four coordinates is inferred.

functions.name: dng_rect::IsZero
functions.description: Returns whether all coordinates of the rectangle are zero. Definition is not provided here; based on naming, it likely checks t==0, l==0, b==0, r==0.
requirements: Rectangle must be a valid initialized dng_rect.

functions.name: dng_rect::W
functions.description: Returns the width of the rectangle. If r >= l, returns (r - l) as an unsigned width, otherwise returns 0. Throws a program error if (r - l) cannot be represented as a signed int32 (even if it fits in uint32), to protect downstream uses that cast to int32.
requirements: Caller must be prepared to handle a ThrowProgramError exception if (r - l) exceeds the range of a signed int32.
If r < l, the function returns 0 without throwing.
No overflow occurs inside when width fits in signed int32.

functions.name: dng_rect::H
functions.description: Returns the height of the rectangle. If b >= t, returns (b - t); otherwise returns 0. Throws a program error if (b - t) cannot be represented as a signed int32 (even if it fits in uint32).
requirements: Caller must be prepared to handle a ThrowProgramError exception if (b - t) exceeds the range of a signed int32.
If b < t, the function returns 0 without throwing.

functions.name: dng_rect::TL
functions.description: Returns the top-left corner of the rectangle as a dng_point (v=t, h=l).
requirements: Rectangle coordinates should be valid int32 values.

functions.name: dng_rect::TR
functions.description: Returns the top-right corner of the rectangle as a dng_point (v=t, h=r).
requirements: Rectangle coordinates should be valid int32 values.

functions.name: dng_rect::BL
functions.description: Returns the bottom-left corner of the rectangle as a dng_point (v=b, h=l).
requirements: Rectangle coordinates should be valid int32 values.

functions.name: dng_rect::BR
functions.description: Returns the bottom-right corner of the rectangle as a dng_point (v=b, h=r).
requirements: Rectangle coordinates should be valid int32 values.

functions.name: dng_rect::Size
functions.description: Returns the rectangle size as a dng_point where v=H() and h=W(). Uses H() and W() internally and casts to int32, which is safe because H() and W() check signed-int32 range.
requirements: Caller must be prepared to handle exceptions from H() or W() if height or width exceed signed int32.
For empty rectangles (r<l or b<t), size components may be 0.

functions.name: dng_rect::Diagonal
functions.description: Returns the Euclidean length of the rectangle’s diagonal using hypot(W(), H()).
requirements: Caller must be prepared to handle exceptions from W() or H() if width or height exceed signed int32.

functions.name: dng_rect_real64::operator==
functions.description: Compares two dng_rect_real64 instances for equality. Body not shown; inferred to compare t, l, b, r for exact equality.
requirements: Input must be a valid dng_rect_real64.
Floating-point equality comparison semantics are not documented; presumed exact bitwise equality of coordinates.

functions.name: dng_rect_real64::IsZero
functions.description: Returns whether all rectangle coordinates are zero. Definition not shown; inferred to test t==0.0, l==0.0, b==0.0, r==0.0.
requirements: Rectangle must be a valid initialized dng_rect_real64.

functions.name: dng_rect_real64::W
functions.description: Returns the width as max(r - l, 0.0). Never throws based on the header; clamps negative widths to 0.
requirements: Inputs should be finite real64 values for meaningful results.

functions.name: dng_rect_real64::H
functions.description: Returns the height as max(b - t, 0.0). Never throws based on the header; clamps negative heights to 0.
requirements: Inputs should be finite real64 values for meaningful results.

functions.name: dng_rect_real64::TL
functions.description: Returns top-left corner as dng_point_real64 (v=t, h=l).
requirements: Coordinates should be finite real64 values.

functions.name: dng_rect_real64::TR
functions.description: Returns top-right corner as dng_point_real64 (v=t, h=r).
requirements: Coordinates should be finite real64 values.

functions.name: dng_rect_real64::BL
functions.description: Returns bottom-left corner as dng_point_real64 (v=b, h=l).
requirements: Coordinates should be finite real64 values.

functions.name: dng_rect_real64::BR
functions.description: Returns bottom-right corner as dng_point_real64 (v=b, h=r).
requirements: Coordinates should be finite real64 values.

functions.name: dng_rect_real64::Size
functions.description: Returns size as dng_point_real64 where v=H() and h=W().
requirements: Coordinates should be finite real64 values; negative extents are clamped to 0 via H()/W().

functions.name: dng_rect_real64::Round
functions.description: Returns an integer dng_rect by rounding each coordinate (t,l,b,r) to int32 using Round_int32.
requirements: Inputs should be within the representable range of Round_int32 for conversion to int32; behavior for out-of-range values is not specified here.
Caller should be prepared for possible exceptions or undefined behavior if rounding cannot produce a valid int32 (documentation of Round_int32 is not included here; exact behavior unknown).

functions.name: dng_rect_real64::Diagonal
functions.description: Returns the Euclidean length of the rectangle’s diagonal as hypot(W(), H()).
requirements: Coordinates should be finite real64 values for meaningful results.

functions.name: operator&
functions.description: Intersection of two integer rectangles. Returns the overlapping area between a and b as a dng_rect.
requirements: Both inputs must be valid dng_rect instances.
If rectangles do not overlap, the result is expected to be empty (IsEmpty()==true). Exact edge semantics are not documented here but standard rectangle intersection is inferred.

functions.name: operator|
functions.description: Union of two integer rectangles. Returns the minimal axis-aligned rectangle containing both a and b.
requirements: Both inputs must be valid dng_rect instances.
Behavior with empty rectangles is not explicitly documented; standard union semantics are inferred.

functions.name: operator+
functions.signature: inline dng_rect operator+(const dng_rect &a, const dng_point &b);
functions.description: Translates rectangle a by point b (v,h). Adds b.v to t and b, and b.h to l and r.
requirements: Inputs must be valid dng_rect and dng_point.
Caller must ensure additions do not overflow int32 when computing new edges.

functions.name: operator+
functions.signature: inline dng_rect_real64 operator+(const dng_rect_real64 &a, const dng_point_real64 &b);
functions.description: Translates rectangle a by point b (v,h) in real64 space. Adds b.v to t and b, and b.h to l and r.
requirements: Inputs must be valid dng_rect_real64 and dng_point_real64.
Coordinates should be finite real64 values.

functions.name: operator-
functions.signature: inline dng_rect operator-(const dng_rect &a, const dng_point &b);
functions.description: Translates rectangle a by the negative of point b. Subtracts b.v from t and b, and b.h from l and r.
requirements: Inputs must be valid dng_rect and dng_point.
Caller must ensure subtractions do not overflow/underflow int32 when computing new edges.

functions.name: operator-
functions.signature: inline dng_rect_real64 operator-(const dng_rect_real64 &a, const dng_point_real64 &b);
functions.description: Translates rectangle a by the negative of point b in real64 space.
requirements: Inputs must be valid dng_rect_real64 and dng_point_real64.
Coordinates should be finite real64 values.

functions.name: Transpose
functions.description: Returns a with vertical and horizontal axes swapped: (t,l,b,r) -> (l,t,r,b).
requirements: Input must be a valid dng_rect.
Caller should ensure swapped coordinates remain within int32 range (values are copied).

functions.name: Transpose
functions.description: Returns a with vertical and horizontal axes swapped in real64.
requirements: Input must be a valid dng_rect_real64.
Coordinates should be finite real64 values.

functions.name: HalfRect
functions.description: In-place scales the rectangle’s width and height by 1/2, keeping the top-left corner fixed. Implemented by setting r = l + (W() >> 1) and b = t + (H() >> 1).
requirements: Input must be a valid dng_rect.
Caller must be prepared for W()/H() to throw if width/height exceed signed int32 before halving.
Resulting coordinates must fit in int32; right/bottom are computed via int32 arithmetic after shifting.

functions.name: DoubleRect
functions.description: In-place scales the rectangle’s width and height by 2, keeping the top-left corner fixed. Implemented by setting r = l + (W() << 1) and b = t + (H() << 1).
requirements: Input must be a valid dng_rect.
Caller must be prepared for W()/H() to throw if initial width/height exceed signed int32.
Caller should ensure that doubling width/height and adding to l/t do not overflow int32.

functions.name: InnerPadRect
functions.description: Shrinks the rectangle in-place by pad on all sides: l+=pad, r-=pad, t+=pad, b-=pad. Negative pad grows the rectangle (but see OuterPadRect for a named wrapper).
requirements: Input must be a valid dng_rect.
Caller should ensure additions/subtractions do not overflow/underflow int32.
Padding may invert the rectangle (make it empty); this is allowed.

functions.name: OuterPadRect
functions.description: Grows the rectangle in-place by pad on all sides by delegating to InnerPadRect with -pad.
requirements: Input must be a valid dng_rect.
Caller should ensure additions/subtractions do not overflow/underflow int32.
Negative pad will shrink the rectangle.

functions.name: InnerPadRectH
functions.description: Shrinks the rectangle horizontally in-place by pad on left and right: l+=pad, r-=pad.
requirements: Input must be a valid dng_rect.
Caller should ensure additions/subtractions do not overflow/underflow int32.
Padding may invert the horizontal extent (empty rectangle).

functions.name: InnerPadRectV
functions.description: Shrinks the rectangle vertically in-place by pad on top and bottom: t+=pad, b-=pad.
requirements: Input must be a valid dng_rect.
