functions.description: Returns the additional gain factor used during stage 3 build.

functions.name: dng_negative::EncodeRawProxy
functions.signature: dng_image * dng_negative::EncodeRawProxy(dng_host &host, const dng_image &srcImage, dng_opcode_list &opcodeList) const
functions.description: Encodes a proxy image from srcImage down to 8 bits/channel adaptively. Returns a newly allocated image; caller owns it.
requirements: host must be a valid dng_host.
srcImage must be a valid image.
Caller must delete/free the returned dng_image when done.

functions.name: dng_negative::ConvertToProxy
functions.signature: void dng_negative::ConvertToProxy(dng_host &host, dng_image_writer &writer, uint32 proxySize, uint64 proxyCount)
functions.description: Converts the negative to a proxy negative, using the writer and optional size/count constraints.
requirements: host must be a valid dng_host.
writer must be a valid dng_image_writer ready to output.

functions.name: dng_negative::SetIsPreview
functions.description: Marks the file as preview (approximations may have been applied during reading).

functions.name: dng_negative::IsPreview
functions.description: Returns true if the file was read using approximations (preview).

functions.name: dng_negative::SetIsDamaged
functions.description: Marks whether the file appears to be damaged.

functions.name: dng_negative::IsDamaged
functions.description: Returns true if the file appears to be damaged.

functions.name: dng_negative::SetTransparencyMask
functions.description: Sets the transparency mask image with optional bit depth (ownership transferred).
requirements: Caller passes an AutoPtr containing a valid dng_image; ownership is transferred and the AutoPtr passed in will be released (do not use it after).

functions.name: dng_negative::TransparencyMask
functions.description: Returns the current transparency mask image, or NULL.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: dng_negative::RawTransparencyMask
functions.description: Returns the grabbed transparency mask when not saving the current mask, or NULL.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: dng_negative::RawTransparencyMaskBitDepth
functions.description: Returns the bit depth for the raw transparency mask if known (0 if unknown).

functions.name: dng_negative::ReadTransparencyMask
functions.description: Reads the transparency mask from the stream using the host and info.
requirements: host must be a valid dng_host.
stream must be readable and positioned appropriately.
info must describe the input.

functions.name: dng_negative::NeedFlattenTransparency
functions.description: Returns true if the transparency mask needs to be flattened into the stage 3 image.
requirements: host must be a valid dng_host.

functions.name: dng_negative::FlattenTransparency
functions.description: Flattens the transparency mask into the stage 3 image, if needed.
requirements: host must be a valid dng_host.
Assumes a stage 3 image is available.

functions.name: dng_negative::UnflattenedStage3Image
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a saved copy of the stage 3 image before transparency flattening, if kept; NULL otherwise.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: dng_function_exposure_ramp::dng_function_exposure_ramp
functions.description: Constructor for an exposure ramp curve used for pre-exposure-compensation adjustment based on noise floor, shadows, and highlight level. Initializes internal parameters to shape a piecewise/rounded ramp between black and white levels. Usage: construct with scene white/black and minimum black levels, then call Evaluate to map input tones.
requirements: white, black, and minBlack are real64 values; valid numeric ranges are not documented in this header (domain constraints unknown).
Object must be constructed before calling Evaluate.

functions.name: dng_function_exposure_ramp::Evaluate
functions.description: Evaluates the exposure ramp curve at input x and returns the mapped tone value. Intended for pre-exposure-compensation adjustment with a rounded ramp shaped by constructor parameters.
requirements: x is real64; the expected input/output range is not documented (domain unknown).
May be called on a valid, constructed instance.

functions.name: dng_function_exposure_tone::dng_function_exposure_tone
functions.description: Constructor for an exposure compensation tone curve defined by a given compensation amount in stops, using a quadratic roll-off in highlights. Usage: construct with an exposure delta (in stops), then call Evaluate to map tones accordingly.
requirements: exposure is specified in stops; may be positive or negative as implied by exposure compensation semantics (exact bounds not documented).
Object must be constructed before calling Evaluate.

functions.name: dng_function_exposure_tone::Evaluate
functions.description: Evaluates the exposure compensation tone curve at input x and returns the mapped tone value. Lower tones use a slope; upper tones use a quadratic roll-off as configured by the exposure setting.
requirements: x is real64; expected domain/range are not documented (domain unknown).
May be called on a valid, constructed instance.

functions.name: dng_tone_curve_acr3_default::Evaluate
functions.description: Evaluates the default ACR3 tone curve at input x and returns the mapped tone. Intended as the standard tone mapping used by ACR 3.
requirements: x is real64; expected input/output range is not documented (domain unknown).
Call on a valid instance (e.g., the singleton returned by Get()).

functions.name: dng_tone_curve_acr3_default::EvaluateInverse
functions.description: Returns the nearest input value for a given output tone x under the default ACR3 tone curve (approximate inverse mapping).
requirements: x is real64; expected input/output range is not documented (domain unknown).
Call on a valid instance (e.g., the singleton returned by Get()).

functions.name: dng_tone_curve_acr3_default::Get
functions.description: Returns a reference to the default ACR3 tone curve function (likely a singleton) for use wherever a dng_1d_function is required.
requirements: Returned reference must not be stored beyond its validity if it refers to a singleton; typical usage is to use it immediately or keep only a reference while the program ensures its lifetime (exact lifetime management not documented).

functions.name: dng_function_gamma_encode::dng_function_gamma_encode
functions.description: Constructor for a gamma encoding curve tied to a specific color space. Use to map linear tones to the encoding gamma of the provided color space.
requirements: Parameter space must refer to a valid dng_color_space object that remains alive for at least as long as the dng_function_gamma_encode instance (stored by reference).

functions.name: dng_function_gamma_encode::Evaluate
functions.description: Evaluates the encoding gamma curve for the associated color space at input x and returns the gamma-encoded tone value.
requirements: x is real64; expected domain/range are not documented (domain unknown).
The dng_function_gamma_encode instance must have been constructed with a valid dng_color_space reference that is still alive.

functions.name: dng_render::dng_render
functions.description: Constructs a renderer used to convert a digital negative (RAW) to a displayable image, using the supplied host for allocation/progress/abort and the supplied digital negative as the source.
requirements: host must be a valid dng_host object that remains alive for the lifetime of the dng_render instance (stored by reference).
negative must be a valid dng_negative object that remains alive for the lifetime of the dng_render instance (stored by const reference).

functions.name: dng_render::~dng_render
functions.description: Destructor for dng_render. Cleans up resources associated with the rendering instance.
requirements: No special caller requirements beyond destroying only instances that were properly constructed.

functions.name: dng_render::SetWhiteXY
functions.description: Sets the white point (chromaticity) used for the conversion pipeline.
requirements: white must be a valid dng_xy_coord value; specific bounds are not documented here.

functions.name: dng_render::WhiteXY
functions.description: Returns the current white point used for conversion.
requirements: May be called at any time on a valid dng_render instance. No additional preconditions documented.

functions.name: dng_render::SetExposure
functions.description: Sets exposure compensation in stops (positive or negative) for rendering.
requirements: exposure is in stops and may be positive or negative as documented; exact bounds not specified.

functions.name: dng_render::Exposure
functions.description: Returns the current exposure compensation (in stops).
requirements: May be called at any time on a valid dng_render instance.

functions.name: dng_render::SetShadows
functions.description: Sets the shadow clip amount used in rendering.
requirements: shadows is a real64; valid range is not documented.

functions.name: dng_render::Shadows
functions.description: Returns the current shadow clip amount.
requirements: May be called at any time on a valid dng_render instance.

functions.name: dng_render::SetToneCurve
functions.description: Sets a custom tone curve (1D function) for tone mapping during conversion.
requirements: curve must refer to a valid dng_1d_function object that remains alive at least until rendering completes or until a different curve is set (stored as a raw pointer to the provided reference).

functions.name: dng_render::ToneCurve
functions.description: Returns the currently configured tone curve function reference.
requirements: A tone curve must have been set or otherwise initialized before calling; otherwise behavior is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: dng_render::SetFinalSpace
functions.description: Sets the final color space in which the resulting image data will be represented.
requirements: space must refer to a valid dng_color_space that remains alive at least until rendering completes or until a different final space is set (stored as a pointer to the provided reference).

functions.name: dng_render::FinalSpace
functions.description: Returns the final color space currently configured for output.
requirements: A final color space must have been set or otherwise initialized before calling; otherwise behavior is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: dng_render::SetFinalPixelType
functions.description: Sets the pixel type of the final image data.
requirements: type must be one of ttByte (default), ttShort, or ttFloat as documented.

functions.name: dng_render::FinalPixelType
functions.description: Returns the currently configured pixel type for the final image data.
requirements: May be called at any time on a valid dng_render instance.

functions.name: dng_render::SetMaximumSize
functions.description: Sets the maximum dimension, in pixels, for the output image. If either output dimension would exceed this maximum, the larger dimension is clamped to this size and the other is scaled to preserve aspect ratio.
requirements: size is in pixels; exact valid range is not documented (must be chosen so that scaling makes sense).

functions.name: dng_render::MaximumSize
functions.description: Returns the maximum allowed output dimension, in pixels, used for scaling during rendering.
requirements: May be called at any time on a valid dng_render instance.

functions.name: dng_render::Render
functions.description: Performs the actual rendering of the associated digital negative into a displayable image and returns the resulting image object.
requirements: The dng_render instance must have been constructed with valid dng_host and dng_negative references that are still alive.
Any desired parameters (white point, exposure, shadows, tone curve, final space, pixel type, maximum size) should be configured before calling for them to take effect.
Caller is responsible for handling the returned dng_image* (ownership/lifetime management behavior is not documented here).

functions.name: dng_resample_function::Extent
functions.description: Abstract kernel API: returns the support extent of the resampling kernel. Typically used to determine how far from a sample the kernel has non-zero weight. Implemented by concrete kernel types.
requirements: Must be called on a valid instance of a class derived from dng_resample_function.
No explicit range or state constraints are documented.
Semantics of the returned value are kernel-defined; callers should treat it as the half-width of non-zero support (in sample units), but exact meaning is unknown from this header.

functions.name: dng_resample_function::Evaluate
functions.description: Abstract kernel API: evaluates the resampling kernel at position x (typically a distance in sample units). Used to compute interpolation weights.
requirements: Must be called on a valid instance of a class derived from dng_resample_function.
Input x is a real64; no explicit range constraints are documented.
Returned value semantics are kernel-defined; may be zero outside Extent(), but this is not guaranteed by this header.

functions.name: dng_resample_bicubic::Extent
functions.description: Bicubic kernel implementation of Extent(). Returns the kernel’s support extent for the built-in bicubic resampler.
requirements: Call on a valid dng_resample_bicubic instance (or via reference).
No additional constraints documented.

functions.name: dng_resample_bicubic::Evaluate
functions.description: Bicubic kernel implementation of Evaluate(). Computes the bicubic kernel’s weight at distance x.
requirements: Call on a valid dng_resample_bicubic instance (or via reference).
Input x is a real64; no explicit range constraints are documented.

functions.name: dng_resample_bicubic::Get
functions.description: Returns a reference to a shared/global bicubic resampling kernel object. Useful for passing a kernel to resampling APIs without constructing an instance.
requirements: The returned reference must not be stored beyond program/library lifetime assumptions; exact lifetime/thread-safety are not specified but typically refer to a static singleton.
No parameters; always returns a valid kernel reference per typical pattern, though not guaranteed by this header.

functions.name: dng_resample_coords::dng_resample_coords
functions.description: Default constructor for the coordinate mapping helper used during resampling. Sets up an empty object; buffers are uninitialized until Initialize is called.
requirements: No arguments; after construction, Initialize must be called before accessing Coords or Pixel.

functions.name: dng_resample_coords::~dng_resample_coords
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the coordinate mapping helper. Releases any owned memory.
requirements: No special requirements for callers.

functions.name: dng_resample_coords::Initialize
functions.signature: void Initialize (int32 srcOrigin, int32 dstOrigin, uint32 srcCount, uint32 dstCount, dng_memory_allocator &allocator);
functions.description: Allocates and computes the integer coordinate table mapping destination indices to source sample positions (with fixed-point subsampling). Must be called before querying Coords or Pixel.
requirements: allocator must be a valid dng_memory_allocator reference capable of allocating the required memory.
srcOrigin, dstOrigin, srcCount, and dstCount must define sensible ranges for the mapping; exact constraints are not documented.
Must be called before Coords or Pixel to ensure fCoords is non-null and indexes are valid.
Behavior for zero or extremely large counts is not specified; callers should avoid pathological values.

functions.name: dng_resample_coords::Coords
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the fixed-point coordinate tuple for the given destination index. Element 0 encodes the source pixel index in fixed-point with kResampleSubsampleBits fractional bits.
requirements: Initialize must have been called successfully so that fCoords is allocated.
index must be within the range of indices for which coordinates were prepared by Initialize; exact bounds are not specified in this header.
Passing an out-of-range index results in pointer arithmetic outside the allocated buffer (undefined behavior).

functions.name: dng_resample_coords::Pixel
functions.description: Returns the integer source pixel index corresponding to the given destination index by right-shifting the fixed-point coordinate by kResampleSubsampleBits.
requirements: Initialize must have been called successfully so that fCoords is allocated.
index must be within the prepared coordinate range from Initialize; exact bounds are not specified.
Relies on Coords(index)[0]; out-of-range index leads to undefined behavior.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights::dng_resample_weights
functions.description: Default constructor for 1D resampling weights. Sets fields to defaults; weights buffers are null until Initialize is called.
requirements: No arguments; Initialize must be called before using Weights32/Weights16 or reading derived parameters that depend on initialization.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights::~dng_resample_weights
functions.description: Virtual destructor for 1D resampling weights. Releases allocated buffers.
requirements: No special requirements for callers.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights::Initialize
functions.signature: void Initialize (real64 scale, const dng_resample_function &kernel, dng_memory_allocator &allocator);
functions.description: Builds 1D resampling weight tables for a given scale and kernel, allocating memory via the provided allocator. Also computes the kernel radius and stepping information.
requirements: allocator must be a valid dng_memory_allocator reference.
kernel must be a valid reference to a live dng_resample_function for the duration of the call.
scale is a real64; the header does not specify constraints (e.g., > 0), so valid ranges are unknown.
Must be called before Weights32/Weights16 are used.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights::Radius
functions.description: Returns the kernel radius used for the 1D weights table (half the filter width in taps).
requirements: Call after Initialize to obtain meaningful data; the header does not specify defaults if uninitialized.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights::Width
functions.description: Returns the filter width in taps (2 * Radius()).
requirements: Call after Initialize to obtain meaningful data.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights::Offset
functions.description: Returns the offset to the first contributing tap, typically 1 - Radius(). Used to align tap indices with source samples.
requirements: Call after Initialize to obtain meaningful data.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights::Step
functions.description: Returns the stride (in elements) between subsample entries in the weights table.
requirements: Call after Initialize to obtain meaningful data.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights::Weights32
functions.description: Provides a pointer to the 32-bit floating-point weight vector for the given fractional subsample position. Performs bounds checking on fract and throws on invalid input.
requirements: Initialize must have been called so that fWeights32 is non-null; otherwise the internal assertion would fail.
fract must be < kResampleSubsampleCount (i.e., 0 <= fract < 128) per this header; otherwise ThrowBadFormat() is called.
Caller must not hold the returned pointer beyond the lifetime of this dng_resample_weights instance.
Returned vector has length Width() and is laid out with stride Step().

functions.name: dng_resample_weights::Weights16
functions.description: Provides a pointer to the 16-bit integer weight vector for the given fractional subsample position. Performs bounds checking on fract and throws on invalid input.
requirements: Initialize must have been called so that fWeights16 is non-null; otherwise the internal assertion would fail.
fract must be < kResampleSubsampleCount (i.e., 0 <= fract < 128) per this header; otherwise ThrowBadFormat() is called.
Caller must not hold the returned pointer beyond the lifetime of this dng_resample_weights instance.
Returned vector has length Width() and is laid out with stride Step().

functions.name: dng_resample_weights_2d::dng_resample_weights_2d
functions.description: Default constructor for 2D resampling weights. Buffers are null until Initialize is called.
requirements: No arguments; Initialize must be called before using Weights32/Weights16 or reading derived parameters that depend on initialization.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights_2d::~dng_resample_weights_2d
functions.description: Virtual destructor for 2D resampling weights. Releases allocated buffers.
requirements: No special requirements for callers.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights_2d::Initialize
functions.description: Builds 2D resampling weight tables for the given kernel, allocating memory via the provided allocator. Also computes the radius and row/column strides for subsampling lookup.
requirements: allocator must be a valid dng_memory_allocator reference.
kernel must be a valid reference to a live dng_resample_function for the duration of the call.
Must be called before Weights32/Weights16 are used.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights_2d::Radius
functions.description: Returns the kernel radius used for the 2D weights table (half the filter width in taps).
requirements: Call after Initialize to obtain meaningful data.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights_2d::Width
functions.description: Returns the filter width in taps (2 * Radius()).
requirements: Call after Initialize to obtain meaningful data.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights_2d::Offset
functions.description: Returns the offset to the first contributing tap, typically 1 - Radius().
requirements: Call after Initialize to obtain meaningful data.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights_2d::RowStep
functions.description: Returns the stride (in elements) between successive fractional rows in the 2D weights table.
requirements: Call after Initialize to obtain meaningful data.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights_2d::ColStep
functions.description: Returns the stride (in elements) between successive fractional columns in the 2D weights table.
requirements: Call after Initialize to obtain meaningful data.

functions.name: dng_resample_weights_2d::Weights32
functions.description: Provides a pointer to the 32-bit floating-point 2D weight block for the given fractional position. Validates that both components of fract are within the permitted subsample range and throws on invalid input.
requirements: Initialize must have been called so that fWeights32 is non-null; otherwise the internal assertion would fail.
fract.v and fract.h must be >= 0 and < kResampleSubsampleCount2D (i.e., 0 <= component < 32); otherwise ThrowBadFormat() is called.
Caller must not hold the returned pointer beyond the lifetime of this dng_resample_weights_2d instance.
Returned block has dimensions derived from Width(); layout uses RowStep() and ColStep().

functions.name: dng_resample_weights_2d::Weights16
functions.description: Provides a pointer to the 16-bit integer 2D weight block for the given fractional position. Validates that both components of fract are within the permitted subsample range and throws on invalid input.
requirements: Initialize must have been called so that fWeights16 is non-null; otherwise the internal assertion would fail.
fract.v and fract.h must be >= 0 and < kResampleSubsampleCount2D (i.e., 0 <= component < 32); otherwise ThrowBadFormat() is called.
Caller must not hold the returned pointer beyond the lifetime of this dng_resample_weights_2d instance.
Returned block has dimensions derived from Width(); layout uses RowStep() and ColStep().

functions.name: ResampleImage
functions.signature: void ResampleImage (dng_host &host, const dng_image &srcImage, dng_image &dstImage, const dng_rect &srcBounds, const dng_rect &dstBounds, const dng_resample_function &kernel);
functions.description: Resamples a region of the source image into a region of the destination image using the specified kernel. The host provides allocation/services needed by the operation. Typical use is to scale, shift, or otherwise resample image data between rectangles.
requirements: host must be a valid dng_host reference for the duration of the call.
srcImage and dstImage must be valid images; exact pixel format and plane requirements are not specified in this header.

srcBounds and dstBounds must be valid rectangles; this header does not specify whether they must lie within the respective image bounds, but callers should provide sensible, in-range rectangles to avoid undefined behavior.
kernel must be a valid dng_resample_function reference for the duration of the call.
Error handling behavior (return codes/exceptions) is not documented here; callers should be prepared for the callee to throw on invalid inputs.

functions.name: EvaluateSplineSegment
functions.signature: inline real64 EvaluateSplineSegment(real64 x, real64 x0, real64 y0, real64 s0, real64 x1, real64 y1, real64 s1);
functions.description: Evaluate a single cubic Hermite spline segment between two knots (x0,y0) and (x1,y1) with endpoint slopes s0 and s1 at position x. Intended for use inside piecewise-spline evaluators; does not depend on any external state. Returns the interpolated value at x; for x outside [x0,x1], the cubic defined by the two endpoints is extrapolated.
requirements: x1 must not equal x0 (division by zero would occur).
All arguments should be valid real numbers (NaN/Inf will propagate through the arithmetic).

functions.name: dng_spline_solver::dng_spline_solver
functions.description: Default constructor for a 1D spline solver that collects sample points and can later solve for spline parameters (e.g., slopes) to evaluate a smooth mapping. No arguments; initializes internal state and empty point arrays.
requirements: No explicit requirements documented.

functions.name: dng_spline_solver::~dng_spline_solver
functions.description: Virtual destructor for dng_spline_solver. Releases any resources owned by the solver and allows safe deletion via base-class pointers.
requirements: No explicit requirements documented.

functions.name: dng_spline_solver::Reset
functions.description: Reset the solver to its initial empty state, clearing any previously added points and computed spline data. Use this to reuse the object for a new set of samples.
requirements: Effect on already-added points or solved state is to clear them (inferred from name).
Subsequent evaluation will typically require re-adding points and calling Solve again (inferred).

functions.name: dng_spline_solver::Add
functions.description: Add a sample point (x,y) to the spline data set. Points are later processed by Solve() to compute a piecewise spline mapping.
requirements: x and y should be valid finite real numbers (inferred).
Typically called before Solve(); adding points after Solve() likely requires another Solve() before Evaluate() (inferred).
The acceptable ordering or uniqueness of x-values is not documented; many spline solvers require strictly increasing and distinct x (unknown here).

functions.name: dng_spline_solver::Solve
functions.description: Compute the internal spline parameters (e.g., segment slopes) from the currently added points so that subsequent Evaluate() calls can interpolate smoothly. Must generally be called after all points are added and before evaluation.
requirements: Should be called after adding the desired set of points (inferred).
At least two points are typically required to define a spline (inferred).
Behavior with duplicate or unsorted x-values is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: dng_spline_solver::IsIdentity
functions.description: Report whether the spline represents an identity mapping (i.e., f(x) == x) under the solver’s current state. Exact criteria are not documented in this header.
requirements: No explicit requirements documented.
Return semantics (exact vs. approximate identity) are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: dng_spline_solver::Evaluate
functions.description: Evaluate the spline at position x using the solution computed by Solve(). Returns the interpolated (or possibly extrapolated) value. Likely uses cubic segments between added knots.
requirements: Typically requires that Solve() has been called after adding points (inferred).
Domain handling for x outside the range of provided points is not documented (unknown).
x should be a valid finite real number to avoid propagating NaNs/Infs (inferred).

functions.name: dng_1d_function::~dng_1d_function
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the abstract 1D floating-point function base class. Ensures proper cleanup through base-class pointers.
requirements: Object must be destroyed via a pointer/reference to dng_1d_function or a derived class with a virtual destructor.
No specific preconditions; safe to call at object lifetime end.

functions.name: dng_1d_function::IsIdentity
functions.description: Returns true if this function is the identity mapping (Evaluate(x) == x for all x). Default implementation may be overridden by derived classes.
requirements: No arguments; callable on any valid instance.
Return value should be used to detect if the function is identity for optimization paths.

functions.name: dng_1d_function::Evaluate
functions.description: Pure virtual method that maps an input x in [0.0, 1.0] to an output y according to the function’s definition. Must be implemented by derived classes.
requirements: x must be between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive.
The derived class must provide a valid implementation that handles the entire [0.0, 1.0] domain.
Implementations should be side-effect free and thread-safe if used concurrently (not explicitly stated but typical for const evaluators).

functions.name: dng_1d_function::EvaluateInverse
functions.description: Computes an x such that Evaluate(x) ≈ y. Default implementation uses Newton’s method to invert Evaluate.
requirements: y should be within the range of the specific function implementation.
Caller should expect a numeric approximation (not exact) due to Newton’s method.
Behavior is undefined if the function is not invertible at y or if y is outside the function’s range (not explicitly specified beyond range note).

functions.name: dng_1d_identity::IsIdentity
functions.description: Always returns true; dng_1d_identity represents the identity mapping.
requirements: No arguments; callable on any valid instance.

functions.name: dng_1d_identity::Evaluate
functions.description: Identity mapping: returns x unchanged.
requirements: x should be between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive (class contract for domain).

functions.name: dng_1d_identity::EvaluateInverse
functions.description: Inverse of the identity is itself: returns y unchanged.
requirements: y should be within the function’s range; for identity this is the same as the input domain range [0.0, 1.0].

functions.name: dng_1d_identity::Get
functions.description: Returns a threadsafe singleton instance of the identity function as a dng_1d_function reference.
requirements: No arguments; safe to call from multiple threads.
Returned reference remains valid for the program’s lifetime (singleton as stated). Do not attempt to delete it.

functions.name: dng_1d_concatenate::dng_1d_concatenate
functions.description: Constructs a function representing the composition y = function2.Evaluate(function1.Evaluate(x)). Values from function1 outside [0.0, 1.0] are pinned to [0.0, 1.0] before applying function2.
requirements: function1 and function2 must remain valid for the lifetime of the dng_1d_concatenate instance (stored as references).
Caller should be aware that outputs of function1 outside [0.0, 1.0] will be clipped to [0.0, 1.0] before applying function2, potentially affecting results.

functions.name: dng_1d_concatenate::IsIdentity
functions.description: Returns true only if both composed functions report IsIdentity() == true.
requirements: Requires a valid constructed instance with valid referenced functions.

functions.name: dng_1d_concatenate::Evaluate
functions.description: Evaluates the composed function: function2.Evaluate(function1.Evaluate(x)), pinning the intermediate to [0.0, 1.0] if necessary.
requirements: x must be between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive.
Caller should expect that if function1.Evaluate(x) < 0.0 it is treated as 0.0, and if > 1.0 it is treated as 1.0 before applying function2.

functions.name: dng_1d_concatenate::EvaluateInverse
functions.description: Computes x such that function2.Evaluate(function1.Evaluate(x)) ≈ y. The header cautions use when the inner function does not have range [0.0, 1.0].
requirements: y should be within the range of function2.Evaluate.
Use with caution if the inner function’s range is not within [0.0, 1.0]; inversion may be unreliable in that case (as warned).

functions.description: Apply the LUT mapping to the specified destination area within the provided pixel buffer. Intended to be called by the opcode engine (possibly multi-threaded).
requirements: buffer must be initialized and cover at least dstArea.
dstArea must lie within imageBounds (inferred from standard processing semantics).
threadIndex is supplied by the caller for multi-threaded coordination (inferred).

functions.name: dng_opcode_MapPolynomial::dng_opcode_MapPolynomial
functions.signature: dng_opcode_MapPolynomial (const dng_area_spec &areaSpec, uint32 degree, const real64 *coefficient);
functions.description: Construct an opcode applying a 1D polynomial function to pixel values over a specified area. The function is f(x) = c0 + x*c1 + x^2*c2 + ... up to the given degree.
requirements: degree must be <= kMaxDegree (8 as defined) and consistent with the provided coefficients.
coefficient must point to at least degree+1 coefficients of type real64.
areaSpec must be valid.

functions.name: dng_opcode_MapPolynomial::dng_opcode_MapPolynomial
functions.description: Construct a MapPolynomial opcode by reading area, degree, and coefficients from a stream.
requirements: stream must be readable and positioned at the start of a well-formed MapPolynomial payload.

functions.name: dng_opcode_MapPolynomial::PutData
functions.description: Serialize the MapPolynomial opcode (area, degree, coefficients) to the provided stream.
requirements: stream must be writable.

functions.name: dng_opcode_MapPolynomial::BufferPixelType
functions.description: Report or select the buffer pixel type required for polynomial mapping.
requirements: imagePixelType must be a valid DNG SDK pixel type identifier (inferred).

functions.name: dng_opcode_MapPolynomial::ModifiedBounds
functions.description: Return the bounds potentially affected by the polynomial mapping; typically the same as imageBounds.
requirements: imageBounds must be a valid rectangle.

functions.name: dng_opcode_MapPolynomial::ProcessArea
functions.signature: virtual void ProcessArea (dng_negative &negative, uint32 threadIndex, dng_pixel_buffer &buffer, const dng_rect &dstArea, const dng_rect &imageBounds);
functions.description: Apply the polynomial mapping to pixels in buffer over dstArea. Designed for threaded execution within the DNG opcode pipeline.
requirements: buffer must be initialized and cover dstArea.
dstArea must lie within imageBounds (inferred).
degree and coefficients must have been set consistently (degree <= 8, coefficient count >= degree+1).

functions.name: dng_opcode_DeltaPerRow::dng_opcode_DeltaPerRow
functions.description: Construct an opcode that adds a per-row delta (offset) to pixels over the specified area. The deltas are supplied as a table of 32-bit floats.
requirements: table must reference a memory block containing per-row float values; the number of entries must be sufficient for the rows addressed by areaSpec (inferred).
areaSpec must be valid.

functions.name: dng_opcode_DeltaPerRow::dng_opcode_DeltaPerRow
functions.description: Construct a DeltaPerRow opcode by deserializing its parameters (area and row-delta table) from a stream.
requirements: stream must be readable and positioned at the start of a well-formed DeltaPerRow payload.
host must be valid and able to allocate needed memory.

functions.name: dng_opcode_DeltaPerRow::PutData
functions.description: Serialize the DeltaPerRow opcode (area and delta table) to the provided stream.
requirements: stream must be writable.

functions.name: dng_opcode_DeltaPerRow::BufferPixelType
functions.description: Report or select the buffer pixel type required for applying per-row deltas.
requirements: imagePixelType must be a valid pixel type identifier (inferred).

functions.name: dng_opcode_DeltaPerRow::ModifiedBounds
functions.description: Return the bounds potentially affected by per-row deltas; typically the same as imageBounds.
requirements: imageBounds must be a valid rectangle.

functions.name: dng_opcode_DeltaPerRow::ProcessArea
functions.signature: virtual void ProcessArea (dng_negative &negative, uint32 threadIndex, dng_pixel_buffer &buffer, const dng_rect &dstArea, const dng_rect &imageBounds);
functions.description: Apply per-row additive offsets to pixels in buffer over dstArea.
requirements: buffer must be initialized and cover dstArea.
dstArea must lie within imageBounds (inferred).
The delta table must have sufficient entries for the rows touched by dstArea (inferred).

functions.name: dng_opcode_DeltaPerColumn::dng_opcode_DeltaPerColumn

functions.description: Construct a DeltaPerColumn opcode by deserializing its parameters (area and column-delta table) from a stream.

functions.name: dng_opcode_DeltaPerColumn::PutData

functions.name: dng_opcode_DeltaPerColumn::BufferPixelType

functions.name: dng_opcode_DeltaPerColumn::ModifiedBounds

requirements: imageBounds must be a valid rectangle.

functions.name: dng_opcode_DeltaPerColumn::ProcessArea
functions.signature: virtual void ProcessArea (dng_negative &negative, uint32 threadIndex, dng_pixel_buffer &buffer, const dng_rect &dstArea, const dng_rect &imageBounds);
functions.description: Apply per-column additive offsets to pixels in buffer over dstArea.
requirements: buffer must be initialized and cover dstArea.

The delta table must have sufficient entries for the columns touched by dstArea (inferred).

functions.name: dng_opcode_ScalePerRow::dng_opcode_ScalePerRow
functions.description: Construct an opcode that multiplies pixels by a per-row scale factor over the specified area. The scales are supplied as a table of 32-bit floats.
requirements: table must reference a memory block containing per-row float scale values; the number of entries must be sufficient for the rows addressed by areaSpec (inferred).
areaSpec must be valid.

functions.name: dng_opcode_ScalePerRow::dng_opcode_ScalePerRow
functions.description: Construct a ScalePerRow opcode by deserializing its parameters (area and row-scale table) from a stream.

functions.name: dng_opcode_ScalePerRow::PutData
functions.description: Serialize the ScalePerRow opcode (area and scale table) to the stream.

functions.name: dng_opcode_ScalePerRow::BufferPixelType
functions.description: Report or select the buffer pixel type required for applying per-row scales.

functions.name: dng_opcode_ScalePerRow::ModifiedBounds
functions.description: Return the bounds potentially affected by per-row scaling; typically the same as imageBounds.

functions.name: dng_opcode_ScalePerRow::ProcessArea
functions.signature: virtual void ProcessArea (dng_negative &negative, uint32 threadIndex, dng_pixel_buffer &buffer, const dng_rect &dstArea, const dng_rect &imageBounds);
functions.description: Apply per-row multiplicative scaling to pixels in buffer over dstArea.
requirements: buffer must be initialized and cover dstArea.
dstArea must lie within imageBounds (inferred).
The scale table must have sufficient entries for the rows touched by dstArea (inferred).

functions.description: Construct an opcode that multiplies pixels by a per-column scale factor over the specified area. The scales are supplied as a table of 32-bit floats.

functions.name: dng_opcode_ScalePerColumn::dng_opcode_ScalePerColumn
functions.description: Construct a ScalePerColumn opcode by deserializing its parameters (area and column-scale table) from a stream.

functions.name: dng_opcode_ScalePerColumn::PutData

functions.name: dng_opcode_ScalePerColumn::ProcessArea

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::dng_opcode_list
functions.description: Constructs an empty list of opcodes intended to be applied at a specific image processing stage (1, 2, or 3). Typical usage is to create a list for a given stage and then Append opcodes before applying them to an image.
requirements: stage must be a valid image processing stage identifier (per comments: 1, 2, or 3).
Constructed object starts empty and not AlwaysApply until SetAlwaysApply is called.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::~dng_opcode_list
functions.description: Destructor for dng_opcode_list. Releases any resources owned by the list, including owned opcode objects.
requirements: No caller-side requirements; ensure no further use of references or pointers obtained from Entry() after the list is destroyed.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::IsEmpty
functions.description: Returns true if the opcode list contains no opcodes.
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::NotEmpty
functions.description: Returns true if the opcode list contains at least one opcode.
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::AlwaysApply
functions.description: Indicates whether this opcode list has been marked to always be applied and is non-empty. Returns true only if SetAlwaysApply() has been called and the list has at least one opcode.
requirements: None; return value depends on internal flag and list emptiness.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::SetAlwaysApply
functions.description: Marks the opcode list so that it should always be applied when processing. This sets an internal flag; AlwaysApply() will still return false if the list is empty.
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::Count
functions.description: Returns the number of opcodes currently contained in the list.
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::Entry
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the opcode at the given index.
requirements: index must be in the range [0, Count() - 1].
The returned reference becomes invalid if the list is cleared or destroyed.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::Entry
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the opcode at the given index.
requirements: index must be in the range [0, Count() - 1].
The returned reference becomes invalid if the list is cleared or destroyed.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::Clear
functions.description: Removes all opcodes from the list.
requirements: All references previously obtained via Entry() are invalidated after this call.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::Swap
functions.description: Swaps the contents of this opcode list with another list, including opcodes and internal state.
requirements: otherList must be a valid dng_opcode_list instance.
All references previously obtained via Entry() from either list may be invalidated or now refer to the other list’s contents.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::MinVersion
functions.description: Computes the minimum DNG version required to support all opcodes in the list. If includeOptional is true, optional opcodes are included in the calculation; otherwise only required opcodes are considered.
requirements: None; behavior depends on opcodes present and includeOptional flag.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::Apply
functions.description: Applies all opcodes in this list to the specified image, using the provided host and corresponding negative. Intended to be called at the processing stage that matches the list’s stage.
requirements: image must be a valid AutoPtr holding a non-null dng_image to be processed.
negative must correspond to the image being processed (per comment: corresponding negative).
host must be a valid dng_host capable of executing the opcodes.
Should be invoked at the pipeline stage matching the list’s stage (1, 2, or 3).
Expect in-place modification of the image held by the AutoPtr; callers should handle any exceptions propagated by opcode execution.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::Append
functions.description: Appends the specified opcode to this list. Ownership of the opcode is transferred to the list via AutoPtr.
requirements: opcode must hold a non-null dng_opcode instance; ownership is transferred and the input AutoPtr will be released/reset by this call.
The opcode should be appropriate for this list’s stage (inferred from class purpose).

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::Spool
functions.description: Serializes the opcode list into a contiguous block of memory. The returned block is heap-allocated and must be deleted by the caller.
requirements: host must be valid for memory/serialization services needed by opcode serialization.
Caller is responsible for deleting the returned dng_memory_block* to avoid leaks.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::FingerprintToStream
functions.description: Writes a fingerprint (hash/signature) of the opcode list to the provided stream, useful for caching or change detection.
requirements: stream must be writable for the length of the fingerprint data.
Caller should ensure stream’s position is set appropriately for writing; function will write at the stream’s current position.

functions.name: dng_opcode_list::Parse
functions.signature: void dng_opcode_list::Parse(dng_host &host, dng_stream &stream, uint32 byteCount, uint64 streamOffset)
functions.description: Reads and parses an opcode list from the given stream starting at streamOffset, reading exactly byteCount bytes. Throws a bad format exception if the opcode stream length does not exactly match byteCount.
requirements: host must be valid to facilitate allocation/creation of opcodes during parsing.
stream must be readable for the entire range [streamOffset, streamOffset + byteCount).
byteCount must exactly match the length of the opcode data in the stream; a mismatch results in a bad format exception.
streamOffset specifies the starting byte offset within the stream; caller must provide a correct offset for the opcode data.

functions.name: dng_opcode::OpcodeID
functions.description: Returns this opcode's numeric ID as defined by dng_opcode_id. Intended for dispatching, serialization, and capability checks.
requirements: The dng_opcode instance must be properly constructed before calling.
No additional preconditions.

functions.name: dng_opcode::MinVersion
functions.description: Returns the minimum DNG version that supports this opcode. Useful when writing or validating opcodes for a target file version.
requirements: The dng_opcode instance must be properly constructed.
No additional preconditions.

functions.name: dng_opcode::Flags
functions.description: Returns the bitmask of opcode flags (e.g., kFlag_Optional, kFlag_SkipIfPreview).
requirements: The dng_opcode instance must be properly constructed.
Interpretation of bits must match the enum values in dng_opcode.

functions.name: dng_opcode::Optional
functions.description: Convenience check that returns true if the opcode is marked optional (kFlag_Optional set).
requirements: The dng_opcode instance must be properly constructed.

functions.name: dng_opcode::SkipIfPreview
functions.description: Returns true if this opcode may be skipped when rendering preview images (kFlag_SkipIfPreview set).
requirements: The dng_opcode instance must be properly constructed.

functions.name: dng_opcode::WasReadFromStream
functions.description: Reports whether this opcode was deserialized from a stream rather than constructed programmatically.
requirements: The dng_opcode instance must be properly constructed.

functions.name: dng_opcode::Stage
functions.description: Returns the image-processing stage (1=original, 2=linearized/trimmed, 3=demosaiced/trimmed) associated with this opcode.
requirements: The dng_opcode instance must be properly constructed.
Callers should interpret only the values 1, 2, or 3.

functions.name: dng_opcode::SetStage
functions.description: Sets the image-processing stage (1, 2, or 3) for this opcode: 1-original data; 2-linearized and active-area-trimmed; 3-demosaiced and active-area-trimmed.
requirements: stage must be one of {1, 2, 3}.
Must be called before applying the opcode to ensure correct pipeline placement.

functions.name: dng_opcode::IsNOP
functions.description: Returns true if, for its current parameters, this opcode has no effect (no operation). Base implementation always returns false; subclasses may override to signal inert states.
requirements: None beyond a valid object instance.

functions.name: dng_opcode::IsValidForNegative
functions.signature: virtual bool dng_opcode::IsValidForNegative (const dng_negative & negative) const
functions.description: Checks whether the opcode is valid for the provided negative. Base implementation returns true. Subclasses can enforce constraints (e.g., color filter array, dimension compatibility).
requirements: negative must refer to a valid, initialized dng_negative object.

functions.name: dng_opcode::PutData
functions.description: Serializes this opcode’s payload to the provided stream when writing. Base class provides default behavior; subclasses extend/override to write specific parameters.
requirements: stream must be valid, writable, and positioned at the desired write offset.
Caller is responsible for writing any surrounding container/headers expected by the file format.
Must be consistent with MinVersion and OpcodeID.

functions.name: dng_opcode::AboutToApply
functions.description: Performs pre-application checks and setup for this opcode with the given host and negative. Returns true if the opcode should be applied; false if it should be skipped (e.g., optional and unsupported).
requirements: host must be a valid dng_host capable of any needed allocations or logging.
negative must be a valid, initialized dng_negative.
Should be called prior to Apply to honor any internal validation/skip logic.

functions.name: dng_opcode::Apply
functions.description: Pure virtual entry point to apply the opcode to the image using the provided host and negative. Subclasses implement the transformation.
requirements: image must reference a valid image compatible with the opcode’s expected stage and buffer type.
Must be called only if AboutToApply returns true.
host and negative must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: dng_opcode_Unknown::PutData
functions.description: Writes the raw, unknown opcode payload back to a stream, preserving forward-compatibility for opcodes not understood by this SDK.
requirements: stream must be valid and writable.
The instance must have been constructed with captured opcode data (read path) to meaningfully write back.

functions.name: dng_opcode_Unknown::Apply
functions.description: Handles application of an unknown opcode. Behavior is not defined in the header; typical handling is to ignore/no-op to preserve image data when the opcode semantics are unknown.
requirements: image must reference a valid image object.
Do not rely on this altering image data; effect is unspecified (likely a no-op).
host and negative must be valid.

functions.name: dng_filter_opcode::BufferPixelType
functions.description: Returns the pixel type the filter expects to operate on. Default passes through the image’s pixel type; filters may override to request a different buffer type.
requirements: imagePixelType should be a valid pixel type as defined in dng_tag_types.h.

functions.name: dng_filter_opcode::ModifiedBounds
functions.description: Returns the effective processing bounds for this filter, typically the intersection of the image area and any region-of-interest the filter imposes. Default returns the input bounds.
requirements: imageBounds must represent the actual bounds of the image to be processed.

functions.name: dng_filter_opcode::SrcRepeat
functions.description: Returns the repeat period (width,height) of any source mosaic pattern the filter assumes. Default is (1,1) meaning no periodicity constraints.
requirements: None.

functions.name: dng_filter_opcode::SrcArea
functions.signature: virtual dng_rect dng_filter_opcode::SrcArea (const dng_rect &dstArea, const dng_rect & imageBounds)
functions.description: Computes the source pixel area required to produce the specified destination area. Default returns dstArea (no expansion). Used to plan tiling/reads.
requirements: dstArea must lie within imageBounds (as documented).
imageBounds must represent the overall image area.

functions.name: dng_filter_opcode::SrcTileSize
functions.signature: virtual dng_point dng_filter_opcode::SrcTileSize (const dng_point &dstTileSize, const dng_rect &imageBounds)
functions.description: Given a desired destination tile size, returns the source tile size needed. Default derives size from SrcArea, typically equal to dstTileSize.
requirements: dstTileSize should be positive in both dimensions and practical for processing.
imageBounds must be the full destination image bounds.

functions.name: dng_filter_opcode::Prepare
functions.signature: virtual void dng_filter_opcode::Prepare (dng_negative & negative, uint32 threadCount, const dng_point & tileSize, const dng_rect & imageBounds, uint32 imagePlanes, uint32 bufferPixelType, dng_memory_allocator & allocator)
functions.description: Optional one-time setup before area processing: allocate per-thread buffers and initialize state for the filter.
requirements: negative must be valid and correspond to the image to be processed.
threadCount must be > 0 and less than or equal to the host’s MaxThreads (per comment).
imagePlanes must be <= kMaxColorPlanes (per comment).
tileSize represents source tile dimensions; edge tiles may be smaller (per comment).
imageBounds is the total image area to process.
bufferPixelType must be a valid pixel type (see dng_tag_types.h).
allocator must be a valid dng_memory_allocator for temporary buffers.

functions.name: dng_filter_opcode::ProcessArea
functions.signature: virtual void dng_filter_opcode::ProcessArea (dng_negative &negative, uint32 threadIndex, dng_pixel_buffer &srcBuffer, dng_pixel_buffer &dstBuffer, const dng_rect &dstArea, const dng_rect &imageBounds)
functions.description: Core filtering operation from source to destination buffers over dstArea. Intended to avoid allocations; use data prepared in Prepare.
requirements: Prepare should be called before the first ProcessArea call to allocate/setup as needed.
threadIndex must be in the range [0, threadCount-1] where threadCount is the value passed to Prepare (per comment).
dstArea must lie within imageBounds (per comment).
srcBuffer must provide pixels covering the required source area for dstArea; dstBuffer must be writable over dstArea.
negative must remain valid for the duration of processing.

functions.name: dng_filter_opcode::Apply
functions.description: Applies the filter opcode to the given image by orchestrating tiling, Prepare, and ProcessArea calls using the provided host.
requirements: image must reference a valid image of a compatible pixel type or one that can be converted to BufferPixelType.
host must be valid and capable of providing threading and temporary memory.
negative must correspond to the image content.

functions.name: dng_inplace_opcode::BufferPixelType
functions.description: Returns the pixel type this in-place operation expects. Default returns the image’s pixel type; overrides may request a different buffer type.
requirements: imagePixelType should be a valid pixel type as defined in dng_tag_types.h.

functions.name: dng_inplace_opcode::ModifiedBounds
functions.description: Returns the effective processing bounds for this in-place operation. Default returns the input bounds.
requirements: imageBounds must represent the actual bounds of the image to be processed.

functions.name: dng_inplace_opcode::Prepare
functions.signature: virtual void dng_inplace_opcode::Prepare (dng_negative & negative, uint32 threadCount, const dng_point & tileSize, const dng_rect & imageBounds, uint32 imagePlanes, uint32 bufferPixelType, dng_memory_allocator & allocator)
functions.description: Optional pre-processing setup for in-place operations: allocate per-thread working memory and initialize state.
requirements: negative must be valid and correspond to the image to be processed.
threadCount must be > 0 and less than or equal to the host’s MaxThreads (per comment).
imagePlanes must be <= kMaxColorPlanes (per comment).
tileSize represents source tile dimensions; edge tiles may be smaller (per comment).
imageBounds is the total image area to process.
bufferPixelType must be a valid pixel type (see dng_tag_types.h).
allocator must be a valid dng_memory_allocator for temporary buffers.

functions.name: dng_inplace_opcode::ProcessArea
functions.signature: virtual void dng_inplace_opcode::ProcessArea (dng_negative &negative, uint32 threadIndex, dng_pixel_buffer &buffer, const dng_rect &dstArea, const dng_rect &imageBounds)
functions.description: Performs the in-place image operation over dstArea, reading and writing the same buffer. Intended to avoid allocations; use any state set up in Prepare.
requirements: Prepare should be called before the first ProcessArea call to allocate/setup as needed.
threadIndex must be in the range [0, threadCount-1] where threadCount is the value passed to Prepare (per comment).
dstArea must lie within imageBounds (per comment).
buffer must be readable and writable over dstArea.
negative must remain valid for the duration of processing.

functions.name: dng_inplace_opcode::Apply
functions.description: Applies the in-place opcode to the given image by orchestrating tiling, Prepare, and ProcessArea calls using the provided host.
requirements: image must reference a valid image of a compatible pixel type or one that can be converted to BufferPixelType.
host must be valid and capable of providing threading and temporary memory.
negative must correspond to the image content.

functions.name: DoZeroBytes
functions.description: Fills a block of memory with zeros by dispatching to the suite function gDNGSuite.ZeroBytes. Intended for fast zeroing of buffers.
requirements: gDNGSuite.ZeroBytes must be initialized (non-null) before calling.
dPtr must be a valid writable pointer to at least count bytes.
count specifies the number of bytes to zero and may be 0.
Pointer alignment requirements (if any) are unknown.

functions.name: DoCopyBytes
functions.signature: inline void DoCopyBytes(const void *sPtr, void *dPtr, uint32 count)
functions.description: Copies count bytes from sPtr to dPtr via gDNGSuite.CopyBytes. Used for raw memory copying.
requirements: gDNGSuite.CopyBytes must be initialized (non-null).
sPtr must point to at least count readable bytes.
dPtr must point to at least count writable bytes.
Behavior for overlapping regions is unknown (assume unspecified).
Pointer alignment requirements (if any) are unknown.

functions.name: DoSwapBytes16
functions.description: Byte-swaps count 16-bit elements in-place via gDNGSuite.SwapBytes16 (e.g., endianness conversion).
requirements: gDNGSuite.SwapBytes16 must be initialized (non-null).
dPtr must point to at least count 16-bit elements writable in-place.
dPtr should be suitably aligned for uint16 (alignment specifics unknown).

functions.name: DoSwapBytes32
functions.description: Byte-swaps count 32-bit elements in-place via gDNGSuite.SwapBytes32 (e.g., endianness conversion).
requirements: gDNGSuite.SwapBytes32 must be initialized (non-null).
dPtr must point to at least count 32-bit elements writable in-place.
dPtr should be suitably aligned for uint32 (alignment specifics unknown).

functions.name: DoSetArea8
functions.signature: inline void DoSetArea8(uint8 *dPtr, uint8 value, uint32 rows, uint32 cols, uint32 planes, int32 rowStep, int32 colStep, int32 planeStep)
functions.description: Sets all elements in a 3D region of 8-bit data to a constant value using strides, via gDNGSuite.SetArea8.
requirements: gDNGSuite.SetArea8 must be initialized (non-null).
dPtr must be a valid writable base pointer for the region.
rows, cols, planes define the iteration extents; they may be zero.
rowStep, colStep, planeStep define strides; units (bytes vs elements) are not specified (unknown).
The described region must be within allocated memory given the strides and extents.

functions.name: DoSetArea16
functions.signature: inline void DoSetArea16(uint16 *dPtr, uint16 value, uint32 rows, uint32 cols, uint32 planes, int32 rowStep, int32 colStep, int32 planeStep)
functions.description: Sets a strided 3D region of 16-bit elements to a constant value via gDNGSuite.SetArea16.
requirements: gDNGSuite.SetArea16 must be initialized (non-null).
dPtr must be valid and writable for the addressed region.
rows, cols, planes specify extents; may be zero.
rowStep, colStep, planeStep define strides; units (elements vs bytes) are unknown.
Alignment appropriate for uint16 may be required (unspecified).

functions.name: DoSetArea32
