Opens the file specified by filename for either reading (output == false) or writing (output == true), providing a dng_stream-compatible interface for subsequent I/O. The bufferSize selects the size of the internal I/O buffer (defaults to 4 KB). Typical usage is to instantiate this object and then perform reads/writes via inherited dng_stream methods. Error/exception behavior on open failures is not specified in this header and is unknown.
requirements: filename: Pathname must be provided in platform syntax (as documented).
output: Set to true to open for writing; false otherwise (reading).
bufferSize: Size of internal buffer in bytes; defaults to 4 KB (symbol kDefaultBufferSize). Exact valid range or minimum/maximum is not specified.
Behavior on invalid path, permissions issues, or open failures is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: dng_file_stream::~dng_file_stream
functions.description: Destructor for dng_file_stream. Releases resources associated with the file-backed stream (e.g., closes the underlying file and disposes any buffers). Normally invoked when the object goes out of scope or is deleted.
requirements: The object must not be used after destruction (no further I/O calls).
Side effects and error behavior during destruction (e.g., flush failures) are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: dng_filter_task::dng_filter_task
functions.description: Constructs a filtering task that reads from a source dng_image and writes results to a destination dng_image. The task can be used with dng_area_task processing to map source areas to destination areas, allocate per-thread buffers in Start, and perform the actual per-area processing in ProcessArea/Process.
requirements: srcImage must remain valid for the entire lifetime of the dng_filter_task instance (stored as a const reference).
dstImage must remain valid and writable for the entire lifetime of the dng_filter_task instance (stored as a non-const reference).

functions.name: dng_filter_task::~dng_filter_task
functions.description: Virtual destructor for dng_filter_task. Ensures proper cleanup through base-class pointers and allows derived classes to release resources.
requirements: The dng_filter_task object must be destroyed only after any referenced srcImage/dstImage remain valid until destruction completes.

functions.name: dng_filter_task::SrcArea
functions.description: Computes the source area required to generate a given destination area. The default implementation returns the destination area unchanged (1:1 mapping). Override in derived classes when the filter requires a different source footprint (e.g., kernels, resampling).
requirements: dstArea must describe a valid rectangular region in destination coordinates.
If overridden, callers should still pass the destination area they intend to compute; the method will return the required source area.

functions.name: dng_filter_task::SrcTileSize
functions.description: Calculates the preferred source tile size needed to produce a destination tile of the requested size. Default behavior computes SrcArea(dng_rect(dstTileSize)).Size(), typically mirroring the destination size. Override if source tiling differs from destination tiling.
requirements: dstTileSize should represent the intended destination tile dimensions.
Behavior depends on SrcArea; if SrcArea is overridden, this result will follow that mapping.

functions.name: dng_filter_task::ProcessArea
functions.signature: virtual void dng_filter_task::ProcessArea(uint32 threadIndex, dng_pixel_buffer &srcBuffer, dng_pixel_buffer &dstBuffer) = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual method that performs the actual filtering from source pixels to destination pixels for a specific area. Called by the framework with per-thread state already set up. No memory allocation should occur here; do work using buffers prepared in Start.
requirements: threadIndex is in the range [0, threadCount - 1] where threadCount is the value passed to Start.
srcBuffer provides the input area and source pixels; it must correspond to the area computed by SrcArea for the current destination area.
dstBuffer provides the output area and storage for destination pixels corresponding to the requested destination area.
Implementations should not allocate memory in this routine; any temporary buffers should be allocated in Start.

functions.name: dng_filter_task::Start
functions.signature: virtual void dng_filter_task::Start(uint32 threadCount, const dng_point &tileSize, dng_memory_allocator *allocator, dng_abort_sniffer *sniffer)
functions.description: Called before processing begins, potentially on multiple threads, to perform setup such as allocating per-thread buffers and initializing state. Provides the planned source tile size and facilities for allocation and cancellation/progress reporting.
requirements: threadCount is the total number of threads that will be used and is less than or equal to MaxThreads of dng_area_task (as stated).
tileSize indicates the size of source tiles that will be processed; edge tiles may be smaller.
allocator is the dng_memory_allocator to use for allocating temporary buffers (must be suitable for any allocations needed by the task).
sniffer may be used to test for user cancellation and to set up progress reporting.

functions.name: dng_filter_task::Process
functions.signature: virtual void dng_filter_task::Process(uint32 threadIndex, const dng_rect &area, dng_abort_sniffer *sniffer)
functions.description: Processes one tile or partitioned area by invoking the filter implementation. This orchestration method should not be overridden by derived classes; override ProcessArea instead. All memory allocations should have been done in Start.
requirements: threadIndex is an index in [0, threadCount - 1] indicating which thread is executing (threadCount was provided to Start).
area defines the tile/region to process; actual processed regions at the image edges can be smaller.
sniffer is used to check for user cancellation and to update progress.
Do not override this function in derived filter tasks; implement the filtering logic in ProcessArea instead.

functions.name: dng_spooler::Spool
functions.signature: virtual void dng_spooler::Spool(const void *data, uint32 count) = 0
functions.description: Abstract output method used during decoding to receive a sequence of bytes. Implementations should write or accumulate exactly count bytes starting at data. Typical usage: subclass dng_spooler and override Spool to append to a buffer, write to a file/stream, or process the bytes as they arrive. This is a pure virtual interface; no default behavior is provided.
requirements: Must be overridden by subclasses; base class provides no implementation.
Implementations must safely handle receiving exactly count bytes from data without reading past the provided range.
If count > 0, data should be a valid, readable pointer to at least count bytes; if count == 0, data may be null or ignored (inferred from conventional C++ patterns).
Implementations should document and honor any thread-safety expectations; none are defined here (unknown).
Implementations should not throw unless documented by the caller’s contract (unknown).

functions.name: DecodeLosslessJPEG
functions.signature: void DecodeLosslessJPEG(dng_stream &stream, dng_spooler &spooler, uint32 minDecodedSize, uint32 maxDecodedSize, bool bug16)
functions.description: Decodes a lossless JPEG bitstream from stream and spools the decoded bytes to spooler. Use when reading lossless JPEG-encoded image data (e.g., in DNG workflows). The decoder may emit up to maxDecodedSize bytes and can validate that the decoded output falls between minDecodedSize and maxDecodedSize. The bug16 flag toggles a compatibility/quirk path for a known 16‑bit decoding issue (exact behavior unspecified in this header).
requirements: stream must supply a valid lossless JPEG bitstream at its current position (inferred from function name and parameters); stream must remain valid for the duration of the call.
spooler must be a valid dng_spooler instance ready to receive decoded output; its Spool method may be called multiple times with chunks of data (inferred).
minDecodedSize and maxDecodedSize define allowable decoded output size bounds; callers should ensure minDecodedSize <= maxDecodedSize (inferred).
The spooler implementation should be able to accept up to maxDecodedSize bytes in total (inferred).
bug16 selects an alternate decoding path for a known issue; exact semantics are unspecified here (unknown).
Error/exception behavior is not documented in this header (unknown).

functions.name: EncodeLosslessJPEG
functions.signature: void EncodeLosslessJPEG(const uint16 *srcData, uint32 srcRows, uint32 srcCols, uint32 srcChannels, uint32 srcBitDepth, int32 srcRowStep, int32 srcColStep, dng_stream &stream)
functions.description: Encodes planar or interleaved image samples provided by srcData into lossless JPEG format and writes the compressed data to stream. Use when generating lossless JPEG-encoded output (e.g., for DNG tiles/strips). The input samples are supplied as uint16 values with a declared bit depth (srcBitDepth). Row/column stepping parameters control how to traverse the input buffer; exact stepping units (samples vs. bytes) are not specified in this header.
requirements: srcData must point to a valid buffer containing image samples addressable using the provided dimensions and stepping (inferred).
srcRows, srcCols, and srcChannels specify the image dimensions and must be consistent with srcData (inferred).
srcBitDepth indicates the number of valid bits per sample stored in the uint16 container; acceptable range is not specified here (unknown).
srcRowStep and srcColStep define how to move between rows and columns in srcData; whether these are in samples or bytes is not specified (unknown).
stream must be a valid, writable dng_stream that will receive the encoded bitstream (inferred).
Behavior on invalid inputs or write failures is not defined in this header (unknown).

functions.name: dng_pthread_attr_init
functions.description: Initializes a thread attribute object for use with dng_pthread_create. Patterned after POSIX pthread_attr_init.
requirements: attr must be a non-null pointer to an uninitialized dng_pthread_attr_t storage location
On success the attribute object must later be destroyed with dng_pthread_attr_destroy

functions.name: dng_pthread_attr_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a thread attribute object previously initialized with dng_pthread_attr_init. Patterned after POSIX pthread_attr_destroy.
requirements: attr must be a non-null pointer to a dng_pthread_attr_t that has been successfully initialized
Do not use the attribute object after destruction

functions.name: dng_pthread_attr_setstacksize
functions.description: Sets the thread stack size in a thread attribute object for future thread creation. POSIX-like semantics are implied.
requirements: attr must be a non-null pointer to an initialized dng_pthread_attr_t
stacksize should be a positive value; extremely small values may be invalid (exact minimum unspecified)

functions.name: dng_pthread_attr_getstacksize
functions.description: Retrieves the configured stack size from a thread attribute object. POSIX-like semantics are implied.
requirements: attr must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized attribute object
stacksize must be a non-null pointer to receive the size

functions.name: dng_pthread_create
functions.signature: int dng_pthread_create(dng_pthread_t *thread, const dng_pthread_attr_t * /* attrs */, void * (*func)(void *), void *arg);
functions.description: Creates a new thread executing start routine func(arg). Attributes may be provided via attrs. Patterned after pthread_create.
requirements: thread must be a non-null pointer to receive the created thread identifier
func must be a non-null pointer to a function with signature void* (void*)
If attrs is non-null, it must point to a valid, initialized attribute object
The start routine should return a pointer value to be retrieved by dng_pthread_join, or call dng_pthread_exit
Resources created by the thread should be cleaned up by the thread function or its joiner

functions.name: dng_pthread_detach
functions.description: Marks a joinable thread as detached, allowing resources to be reclaimed when it terminates without a join. POSIX-like semantics are implied.
requirements: thread must be a valid thread identifier
Do not call dng_pthread_join on a detached thread

functions.name: dng_pthread_join
functions.description: Waits for the specified thread to terminate and optionally retrieves its exit value. Patterned after pthread_join.
requirements: thread must be a valid joinable (not detached) thread identifier
If result is non-null, it must point to storage for a void* to receive the thread’s return value or the value passed to dng_pthread_exit
Do not attempt to join the calling thread itself

functions.name: dng_pthread_self
functions.description: Returns the identifier of the calling thread. Patterned after pthread_self.
requirements: No arguments; must be called from a valid thread context

functions.name: dng_pthread_exit
functions.description: Terminates the calling thread and makes result available to a potential joiner. Patterned after pthread_exit.
requirements: May only be called by a running thread to terminate itself
If another thread will join this thread, result should be a valid pointer value or NULL as appropriate
Resources requiring cleanup should be released prior to calling unless cleanup handlers/destructors are relied upon

functions.name: dng_pthread_mutexattr_init
functions.description: Initializes a mutex attribute object. Patterned after pthread_mutexattr_init.
requirements: mutexattr must be a non-null pointer to storage for a mutex attribute object
Destroy or stop using attributes when no longer needed (destroy function not declared here)

functions.name: dng_pthread_mutexattr_settype
functions.description: Sets the mutex type on a mutex attribute object (e.g., recursive). DNG_PTHREAD_MUTEX_RECURSIVE is defined. Patterned after pthread_mutexattr_settype.
requirements: mutexattr must be a non-null pointer to an initialized mutex attribute object
Type value must be one of the supported options (exact set unspecified; DNG_PTHREAD_MUTEX_RECURSIVE defined)

functions.name: dng_pthread_mutex_init
functions.description: Initializes a mutex object, optionally with attributes. Patterned after pthread_mutex_init.
requirements: mutex must be a non-null pointer to storage for a mutex object; it may be set to DNG_PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER for static initialization
If attrs is non-null, it must point to a compatible attribute object
A mutex must be destroyed with dng_pthread_mutex_destroy when no longer needed

functions.name: dng_pthread_mutex_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a mutex object previously initialized. Patterned after pthread_mutex_destroy.
requirements: mutex must be a non-null pointer to an initialized mutex
The mutex must be unlocked at the time of destruction
Do not use the mutex after destruction

functions.name: dng_pthread_mutex_lock
functions.description: Locks the specified mutex, blocking if necessary. Patterned after pthread_mutex_lock.
requirements: mutex must be a non-null pointer to an initialized mutex object

functions.name: dng_pthread_mutex_unlock
functions.description: Unlocks the specified mutex. Patterned after pthread_mutex_unlock.
requirements: mutex must be a non-null pointer to an initialized mutex object
Calling thread should hold the lock prior to unlocking

functions.name: dng_pthread_cond_init
functions.description: Initializes a condition variable, optionally with attributes. Patterned after pthread_cond_init.
requirements: cond must be a non-null pointer to storage for a condition variable; it may be set to DNG_PTHREAD_COND_INITIALIZER for static initialization
If attrs is non-null, it must point to a compatible attribute object
Condition variable must be destroyed with dng_pthread_cond_destroy when no longer needed

functions.name: dng_pthread_cond_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a condition variable previously initialized. Patterned after pthread_cond_destroy.
requirements: cond must be a non-null pointer to an initialized condition variable
Do not use the condition variable after destruction

functions.name: dng_pthread_cond_wait
functions.description: Atomically releases the mutex and waits on the condition; upon wakeup, re-acquires the mutex before returning. Patterned after pthread_cond_wait.
requirements: cond must be a non-null pointer to an initialized condition variable
mutex must be a non-null pointer to an initialized mutex that is locked by the calling thread prior to the call
The mutex will be re-locked upon successful return

functions.name: dng_pthread_cond_timedwait
functions.description: Like dng_pthread_cond_wait, but will time out at or after the specified time. Patterned after pthread_cond_timedwait; ETIMEDOUT may be returned on timeout.
requirements: cond must be a non-null pointer to an initialized condition variable
mutex must be a non-null pointer to an initialized mutex that is locked by the calling thread prior to the call
latest_time must be a non-null pointer to a timespec specifying the timeout; semantics are inferred to be an absolute time (POSIX pattern)
On timeout, caller should handle an ETIMEDOUT-style error code

functions.name: dng_pthread_cond_signal
functions.description: Unblocks at least one thread waiting on the condition variable. Patterned after pthread_cond_signal.
requirements: cond must be a non-null pointer to an initialized condition variable
Should be called while holding the associated mutex to avoid race conditions (usage pattern)

functions.name: dng_pthread_cond_broadcast
functions.description: Unblocks all threads waiting on the condition variable. Patterned after pthread_cond_broadcast.
requirements: cond must be a non-null pointer to an initialized condition variable
Should be called while holding the associated mutex to avoid race conditions (usage pattern)

functions.name: dng_pthread_once
functions.description: Ensures that init_func is executed exactly once across all threads for the given control object. Patterned after pthread_once.
requirements: once must be a non-null pointer to a control object, which may be statically initialized with DNG_PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT
init_func must be a non-null pointer to a function taking no arguments and returning void
Do not manually reset the once state after successful initialization

functions.name: dng_pthread_key_create
functions.description: Creates a thread-specific data key, optionally with a per-thread destructor for non-null values. Patterned after pthread_key_create.
requirements: key must be a non-null pointer to receive the created key
destructor, if provided, must be a function taking void* and returning void; it may be NULL (inferred POSIX pattern)

functions.name: dng_pthread_key_delete
functions.description: Deletes a thread-specific data key. Patterned after pthread_key_delete.
requirements: key must be a valid key previously created by dng_pthread_key_create
After deletion, existing per-thread values for the key become inaccessible via this API

functions.name: dng_pthread_setspecific
functions.description: Sets the calling thread’s value for the specified thread-specific data key. Patterned after pthread_setspecific.
requirements: key must be a valid key previously created by dng_pthread_key_create
Value may be any pointer-sized value, including NULL; if non-NULL and a destructor was specified at key creation, it may be run at thread exit (POSIX pattern)

functions.name: dng_pthread_getspecific
functions.description: Retrieves the calling thread’s value for the specified thread-specific data key. Patterned after pthread_getspecific.
requirements: key must be a valid key previously created by dng_pthread_key_create

functions.name: dng_pthread_rwlock_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a read-write lock object previously initialized. Patterned after pthread_rwlock_destroy.
requirements: rwlock must be a non-null pointer to an initialized read-write lock
The lock should not be held by any thread at destruction

functions.name: dng_pthread_rwlock_init
functions.description: Initializes a read-write lock object, optionally with attributes. Patterned after pthread_rwlock_init.
requirements: rwlock must be a non-null pointer to storage for a read-write lock
If attrs is non-null, it must point to a compatible attribute object

functions.name: dng_pthread_rwlock_rdlock
functions.description: Acquires the read lock, allowing shared (reader) access. Patterned after pthread_rwlock_rdlock.
requirements: rwlock must be a non-null pointer to an initialized read-write lock

functions.name: dng_pthread_rwlock_tryrdlock
functions.description: Attempts to acquire the read lock without blocking. Patterned after pthread_rwlock_tryrdlock.
requirements: rwlock must be a non-null pointer to an initialized read-write lock

functions.name: dng_pthread_rwlock_trywrlock
functions.description: Attempts to acquire the write lock without blocking. Patterned after pthread_rwlock_trywrlock.
requirements: rwlock must be a non-null pointer to an initialized read-write lock

functions.name: dng_pthread_rwlock_unlock
functions.description: Releases a held read or write lock. Patterned after pthread_rwlock_unlock.
requirements: rwlock must be a non-null pointer to an initialized read-write lock
The calling thread should currently hold the lock (read or write)

functions.name: dng_pthread_rwlock_wrlock
functions.description: Acquires the write lock, allowing exclusive access. Patterned after pthread_rwlock_wrlock.
requirements: rwlock must be a non-null pointer to an initialized read-write lock

functions.name: dng_pthread_disassociate
functions.description: Frees per-thread global state maintained by the dng_pthread layer. The comment notes it is not necessary for threads created by dng_pthread, and that state will be lazily recreated; avoid calling while holding a mutex. On non-Windows builds this may be a no-op macro.
requirements: Should not be called while holding a mutex or other synchronization object (explicitly stated)
May be called multiple times; state will be recreated as needed (slight performance cost; per comment)

functions.name: dng_pthread_terminate
functions.description: Terminates or tears down dng_pthread internal state. Exact behavior is not documented here; on non-Windows builds this may be a no-op macro. Details unknown beyond name and placement.
requirements: Should not be called while holding synchronization primitives (precaution inferred from similar teardown operations; exact requirement not stated)
Intended for use in controlled shutdown scenarios; exact calling order and effects are unknown

functions.name: dng_pthread_now
functions.description: Obtains the current time and stores it in the provided timespec. Likely used to build absolute timeouts for dng_pthread_cond_timedwait. Exact clock base is not specified; POSIX-style semantics implied.
requirements: now must be a non-null pointer to a struct timespec to receive the current time

functions.name: dng_camera_profile_info::dng_camera_profile_info
functions.description: Constructor. Initializes a camera profile info record to defaults so it can accumulate profile-related TIFF/DNG tag data during parsing.
requirements: Object must be default-constructed before calling other member functions like ParseTag or ParseExtended.

functions.name: dng_camera_profile_info::~dng_camera_profile_info
functions.description: Destructor. Releases any resources owned by the camera profile info record. No special action required by callers.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.

functions.name: dng_camera_profile_info::ParseTag
functions.signature: bool ParseTag(dng_stream &stream, uint32 parentCode, uint32 tagCode, uint32 tagType, uint32 tagCount, uint64 tagOffset);
functions.description: Parses a single TIFF/DNG tag related to the camera profile from the provided stream and records its data/offsets into this profile info. Intended to be called while iterating tags in relevant IFDs for profile data.
requirements: stream must be a valid, readable dng_stream positioned for random-access reads; tagOffset must refer to data within the stream.
parentCode, tagCode, tagType, and tagCount must come from a valid IFD entry; values must match the layout of the underlying file.
Caller should subsequently call ParseExtended to load any deferred/offset-based tables recorded by this pass, if needed.
Returns true if the tag was recognized/consumed by this parser; false if the tag does not belong to this profile or could not be parsed.

functions.name: dng_camera_profile_info::ParseExtended
functions.description: Processes any deferred camera profile data referenced by offsets collected during ParseTag (e.g., hue/sat maps, tone curves, look tables) by reading them from the stream. Use after the first pass over tags.
requirements: Must be called after one or more successful ParseTag calls have populated offset/count members in this object.
stream must be valid and readable; all previously stored offsets/counts must reference data within the stream.
Returns true on success; false if required referenced data is missing or invalid.

functions.name: dng_shared::dng_shared
functions.description: Constructor. Initializes shared DNG metadata/state used during parsing of EXIF, XMP, profiles, and related structures.
requirements: Object must be default-constructed before invoking ParseTag/PostParse/IsValidDNG.

functions.name: dng_shared::~dng_shared
functions.description: Virtual destructor. Allows safe cleanup via base-class pointer after parsing/processing shared DNG metadata.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.

functions.name: dng_shared::ParseTag
functions.signature: virtual bool ParseTag(dng_stream &stream, dng_exif &exif, uint32 parentCode, bool isMainIFD, uint32 tagCode, uint32 tagType, uint32 tagCount, uint64 tagOffset, int64 offsetDelta);
functions.description: Parses a single TIFF/DNG tag into the shared DNG metadata object, optionally updating the provided EXIF structure. Designed to be called while scanning IFD entries across main and subsidiary IFDs.
requirements: stream must be a valid, readable dng_stream supporting random-access reads; tagOffset must reference data within the stream/file.

Returns true if the tag is recognized and parsed by this object; false if unhandled by this parser.

functions.name: dng_shared::PostParse
functions.description: Performs post-processing after all relevant tags have been parsed, finalizing shared metadata (e.g., resolving offsets, computing derived values, validating consistency).

host must be a valid dng_host providing any services needed during finalization.
exif must be a valid, populated dng_exif object corresponding to the parsed data.

functions.name: dng_shared::IsValidDNG
functions.description: Checks whether the currently parsed/shared metadata represents a valid DNG according to required tags/constraints. Returns true if the object state is consistent with a valid DNG.
requirements: Should be called after parsing (and ideally after PostParse) to reflect final state.
Returns true if valid, false otherwise.

functions.name: dng_tone_curve::dng_tone_curve
functions.description: Default constructor for a 1-dimensional tone-curve object. Creates a new curve instance; internal state/details are not documented in this header. Typically used before populating control points or calling state-mutating methods.

functions.name: dng_tone_curve::IsValid

functions.description: Solves or fits the tone curve using the provided dng_spline_solver. Intended to compute spline parameters from the curve’s internal control points/coordinates. The specific algorithm, required point layout, and side effects on the solver are not described here.

functions.name: RoundUpForPixelSize
functions.signature: inline bool RoundUpForPixelSize (uint32 x, uint32 pixelSize, uint32 *result)
functions.description: Rounds x up to a multiple suitable for scanline alignment based on pixelSize. For pixel sizes 1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes, it rounds up to a multiple of 16/pixelSize; otherwise to a multiple of 16. Returns true on success via RoundUpUint32ToMultiple.
requirements: result must be a valid non-null pointer to receive the rounded value.
pixelSize of 1, 2, 4, or 8 selects multiple 16/pixelSize; other values default to multiple 16.
May fail and return false if RoundUpUint32ToMultiple fails (e.g., due to overflow).

requirements: tileSize.h and tileSize.v (components of dng_point) must be non-negative; negative values cause an exception.
Computation may throw on arithmetic overflow; callers should be prepared to handle dng_exception.
pixelType is a code identifying pixel format (exact values not specified here).
numPlanes is the number of image planes; must be appropriate for the pixelType (not specified here).
paddingType controls scanline padding (padNone or pad16Bytes).

functions.name: Round_int32
functions.description: Rounds a 32-bit float to the nearest int32 using round-half-away-from-zero semantics for positive/negative values.

functions.name: Round_int32
functions.description: Rounds a 64-bit float to the nearest int32 using round-half-away-from-zero semantics. Throws a program error on overflow or NaN handling path that exceeds int32 range.
requirements: x must be within (int32_min-1, int32_max+1) after applying ±0.5 offset to avoid ThrowProgramError.

functions.name: Floor_uint32
functions.description: Floors a 32-bit float to an unsigned 32-bit integer, clamping negatives to 0.

functions.name: Floor_uint32
functions.description: Floors a 64-bit float to an unsigned 32-bit integer, clamping negatives to 0. Throws a program error if the floored value is >= 2^32.
requirements: After clamping with Max(0.0, x), the value must be < uint32_max + 1.0 to avoid ThrowProgramError.

functions.name: Round_uint32
functions.description: Rounds a 32-bit float to the nearest uint32 by computing Floor_uint32(x + 0.5f).
requirements: Implicitly subject to Floor_uint32(real32) behavior (negative rounds to 0).

functions.name: Round_uint32
functions.description: Rounds a 64-bit float to the nearest uint32 by computing Floor_uint32(x + 0.5).
requirements: Subject to Floor_uint32(real64) limits; overflowing values will trigger ThrowProgramError via Floor_uint32.

functions.name: Round_int64
functions.description: Rounds a 64-bit float to the nearest int64 using round-half-away-from-zero semantics.

functions.name: Real64ToFixed64
functions.description: Converts a real64 to 32.32 fixed-point (Q32.32) by multiplying by 2^32 and rounding to int64.

functions.name: Fixed64ToReal64
functions.description: Converts a 32.32 fixed-point value (int64) to real64 by dividing by 2^32.

functions.name: ForceUppercase
functions.description: Converts ASCII lowercase letters 'a'..'z' to uppercase; leaves other bytes unchanged.

functions.name: SwapBytes16
functions.description: Swaps the byte order of a 16-bit unsigned integer.

functions.name: SwapBytes32
functions.description: Swaps the byte order of a 32-bit unsigned integer.

functions.name: IsAligned16
functions.description: Returns true if pointer p is 16-bit (2-byte) aligned.
requirements: p may be null; alignment check uses its integer value.

functions.name: IsAligned32
functions.description: Returns true if pointer p is 32-bit (4-byte) aligned.
requirements: p may be null; alignment check uses its integer value.

functions.name: IsAligned64
functions.description: Returns true if pointer p is 64-bit (8-byte) aligned.
requirements: p may be null; alignment check uses its integer value.

functions.name: IsAligned128
functions.description: Returns true if pointer p is 128-bit (16-byte) aligned.
requirements: p may be null; alignment check uses its integer value.

functions.name: DNG_RGBtoHSV
functions.signature: inline void DNG_RGBtoHSV (real32 r, real32 g, real32 b, real32 &h, real32 &s, real32 &v)
functions.description: Converts RGB in [0,1] to HSV where h is in [0,6), s in [0,1], v in [0,1]. Handles gray (gap==0) by setting s=0 and h=0.
requirements: Outputs h, s, v must be valid references.

functions.name: DNG_HSVtoRGB
functions.signature: inline void DNG_HSVtoRGB (real32 h, real32 s, real32 v, real32 &r, real32 &g, real32 &b)
functions.description: Converts HSV (h in [0,6), s in [0,1], v in [0,1]) to RGB in [0,1]. For s==0, outputs gray. For s>0, requires finite h; non-finite h triggers a program error.
requirements: If s > 0, h must be finite (neither NaN nor Inf), otherwise ThrowProgramError is called.
Outputs r, g, b must be valid references.

functions.name: TickTimeInSeconds
functions.description: High-resolution timer for profiling; returns current time in seconds (implementation-defined).

functions.name: TickCountInSeconds
functions.description: Lower-resolution but more stable timer; returns current time in seconds (implementation-defined).

functions.name: MaxSquaredDistancePointToRect
functions.description: Returns the maximum squared Euclidean distance from a point to the rectangle rect.

functions.name: MaxDistancePointToRect
functions.description: Returns the maximum Euclidean distance from a point to the rectangle rect.

functions.name: DNG_HalfToFloat
functions.description: Converts a 16-bit IEEE-754 half-precision value to a 32-bit IEEE-754 single-precision bit pattern (returned as uint32). Special cases: zeros, denormals (renormalized), infinities (mapped to max 16-bit representable float), NaNs map to 0.

functions.name: DNG_FloatToHalf
functions.description: Converts a 32-bit IEEE-754 single-precision bit pattern (uint32) to a 16-bit half-precision representation. Handles zeros/denormals, infinities, and NaNs with reasonable mappings and rounding-to-nearest (ties up).

functions.name: DNG_FP24ToFloat
functions.description: Converts a custom 24-bit floating-point value (3 bytes at input) to a 32-bit IEEE-754 single-precision bit pattern (uint32). Handles zeros, denormals (renormalized), infinities (mapped to max 24-bit representable float), and NaNs (map to 0).
requirements: input must point to at least 3 readable bytes.

functions.name: DNG_FloatToFP24
functions.description: Converts a 32-bit IEEE-754 single-precision bit pattern (uint32) to a custom 24-bit float stored in 3 bytes at output. Handles infinities/NaNs and over/underflow with clamping/denorm encoding; rounds to nearest (ties up).
requirements: output must point to at least 3 writable bytes.

functions.name: DNG_Random
functions.description: Park–Miller minimal standard RNG step compatible with Apple’s implementation. Returns the next 31-bit positive state in [1, 2147483646].

functions.name: dng_dither::Get
functions.description: Returns a singleton instance of dng_dither providing access to a precomputed noise buffer used for dithering.

functions.name: dng_dither::NoiseBuffer16
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal 16-bit noise buffer for dithering. The buffer has size kRNGSize2D elements.
requirements: Returned pointer remains valid as long as the singleton dng_dither instance lives; do not free it.
Data is read-only; do not modify the returned buffer.

functions.name: HistogramArea
functions.signature: void HistogramArea (dng_host &host, const dng_image &image, const dng_rect &area, uint32 *hist, uint32 histLimit, uint32 plane = 0)
functions.description: Computes a histogram over a rectangular area of an image for the specified plane, writing counts into hist up to histLimit bins.
requirements: host must be a valid dng_host ready to access the image.
image must be valid and accessible through host.
area must be within the bounds of image (not specified here, but typically required).
hist must point to an array of at least histLimit uint32 entries.
plane selects the image plane to analyze; must be in range for the image.

functions.name: LimitFloatBitDepth
functions.signature: void LimitFloatBitDepth (dng_host &host, const dng_image &srcImage, dng_image &dstImage, uint32 bitDepth, real32 scale = 1.0f)
functions.description: Reduces or limits the effective bit depth of a floating-point image, writing the result to dstImage. Optionally scales by 'scale'.
requirements: host must be valid for image processing.
srcImage and dstImage must be initialized; dstImage must be allocated/compatible for output.
bitDepth specifies the target bit depth; exact accepted values are not documented here.
scale is a multiplier applied during processing.

functions.name: dng_xmp::dng_xmp
functions.description: Constructor creating an XMP container bound to a memory allocator and internal XMP SDK instance. Use this to start an empty/placeholder XMP object before parsing or setting properties.
requirements: allocator must be a valid, live dng_memory_allocator reference for the lifetime of the dng_xmp instance.
No XMP data is present until Parse is called or properties are set.

functions.name: dng_xmp::dng_xmp
functions.description: Copy constructor. Creates a new dng_xmp instance as a deep copy (including metadata state) of another.
requirements: xmp must refer to a valid, initialized dng_xmp instance.

functions.name: dng_xmp::~dng_xmp
functions.description: Destructor. Releases any internal XMP SDK resources and memory owned by the instance.
requirements: All external pointers previously returned (e.g., via GetPrivateMeta) must not be used after the dng_xmp instance is destroyed.

functions.name: dng_xmp::Clone
functions.description: Virtual constructor. Produces a heap-allocated copy of this dng_xmp. Caller owns the returned pointer.
requirements: Caller must delete the returned pointer when done.
The object being cloned must be valid (i.e., not already destructed).

functions.name: dng_xmp::Parse
functions.signature: void dng_xmp::Parse (dng_host &host, const void *buffer, uint32 count)
functions.description: Parses an XMP packet from a raw buffer and loads it into this dng_xmp instance.
requirements: host must be a valid dng_host reference.
If count > 0, buffer must point to at least count bytes of readable memory.
The buffer must contain XMP serialized data (typically RDF/XML).
Any previously loaded metadata in this instance may be replaced by the parsed content.

functions.name: dng_xmp::Serialize
functions.signature: dng_memory_block * dng_xmp::Serialize (bool asPacket = false, uint32 targetBytes = 0, uint32 padBytes = 4096, bool forJPEG = false, bool compact = true) const
functions.description: Serializes the current XMP metadata to a newly allocated memory block. Options control packet framing, target/pad size, JPEG-specific formatting, and compactness.
requirements: The dng_xmp instance must contain valid metadata (HasMeta can be used to check).
Returned pointer is owned by the caller and must be released according to the SDK’s memory management conventions.
targetBytes and padBytes are sizes in bytes and must fit in uint32. Semantics of targetBytes/padding are SDK-defined (details not provided here).
If forJPEG is true, serialization must meet JPEG APP1/XMP layout expectations (handled internally).

functions.name: dng_xmp::SerializeNonCompact
functions.description: Convenience wrapper that serializes XMP in a non-compact form (workaround for legacy host compatibility).
requirements: Same ownership and validity requirements as Serialize.
Intended for legacy compatibility where non-compact XMP is required.

functions.name: dng_xmp::PackageForJPEG
functions.description: Packages XMP for embedding in JPEG, producing standard and (if needed) extended XMP blocks and their digest for APP1 segments.
requirements: stdBlock and extBlock are output holders and must be valid AutoPtr references; any existing contents may be overwritten.
extDigest is an output parameter that will receive the extended XMP digest if an extended block is produced.
Caller is responsible for embedding the produced blocks into the appropriate JPEG segments.

functions.name: dng_xmp::MergeFromJPEG
functions.description: Merges XMP from a JPEG-sourced dng_xmp into this instance, reconciling standard and extended packets.
requirements: xmp must contain metadata previously parsed or packaged for JPEG.
The current instance will be modified to include or reconcile data from xmp.

functions.name: dng_xmp::HasMeta
functions.description: Returns true if this instance currently contains any XMP metadata.

functions.name: dng_xmp::GetPrivateMeta
functions.description: Returns an opaque pointer to the underlying XMP SDK metadata object for advanced/SDK-specific operations. Details are intentionally hidden.
requirements: The returned pointer is for advanced use; its type and lifetime semantics are SDK-internal and undocumented here (unknown specifics).
Caller must not assume ownership and must avoid using it after the dng_xmp is destroyed.

functions.description: Iterates over property paths in the metadata, calling the provided callback for each match. Namespace and path may filter the iteration.
requirements: callback must be a valid function/callable matching IteratePathsCallback signature (not defined here; unknown specifics).
callbackData is passed through to the callback and may be null.
If ns is non-null, it must be a valid namespace URI; if path is non-null, it must be a valid property path.
The callback must not mutate the dng_xmp in ways that invalidate iteration (behavior unspecified; avoid unless documented).

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

def _rand_utf8_string(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 256) -> bytes:
    # Generate a valid UTF-8 string with a mix of ASCII, Latin-1, BMP, and some emoji
    parts: List[str] = []
    target_len = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    while len("".join(parts)) < target_len:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.55:
            # printable ASCII
            ch = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " .,_-:/\\\t\n\r")
            parts.append(ch)
        elif choice < 0.80:
            # Latin-1 supplement range
            parts.append(chr(rng.randint(0x00A0, 0x00FF)))
        elif choice < 0.96:
            # Basic Multilingual Plane (avoid surrogates)
            code = rng.randint(0x0100, 0xD7FF)
            parts.append(chr(code))
        else:
            # A few emoji code points
            parts.append(rng.choice(["😀", "🎉", "📷", "✨", "🖼️", "🧪"]))
    s = "".join(parts)
    # Ensure we stay within max bytes; trim if necessary
    b = s.encode('utf-8', 'strict')
    if len(b) > max_len:
        # Trim by characters to avoid splitting sequence
        trimmed = []
        total = 0
        for ch in s:
            cb = ch.encode('utf-8')
            if total + len(cb) > max_len:
                break
            trimmed.append(ch)
            total += len(cb)
        b = "".join(trimmed).encode('utf-8')
    return b + b"\x00"  # NUL-terminate


def _rand_ascii_string(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 256) -> bytes:
    length = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " .,_-:/\\\t\n\r"
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    return s.encode('ascii') + b"\x00"


def _make_header(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compose a small header that a fuzzer harness might parse for integers
    # Provide a few random 32-bit integers that stubs use via FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
    ints = [rng.getrandbits(32) for _ in range(8)]
    return b"".join(struct.pack("<I", x) for x in ints)


def _multi_strings_blob(rng: random.Random, count: int, max_each: int) -> bytes:
    data = bytearray()
    for _ in range(count):
        # Mix ASCII-only and full UTF-8 strings
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            data += _rand_ascii_string(rng, max_each)
        else:
            data += _rand_utf8_string(rng, max_each)
    return bytes(data)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Strategy: Provide a stream of bytes that FUZZ_PARAM_STR() can slice sequentially.
    # Include:
    #  - A small integer header for FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
    #  - Several UTF-8 strings (NUL-terminated) to feed dng_string operations
    #  - Some binary chunks for copy/swap tests
    #  - Keep under 4096 bytes

    out = bytearray()

    # 1) Integer header (for flags, sizes, etc.)
    out += _make_header(rng)

    # 2) A bundle of NUL-terminated strings to exercise dng_string paths
    out += _multi_strings_blob(rng, count=12, max_each=128)

    # 3) Additional longer strings (including many digits and separators) for NormalizeAsCommaSeparatedNumbers
    def numericish(r: random.Random, nmax: int) -> bytes:
        chars = []
        length = r.randint(16, nmax)
        sep = [',', ';', ' ', '/', '\t']
        digits = string.digits
        for _ in range(length):
            if r.random() < 0.75:
                chars.append(r.choice(digits))
            else:
                chars.append(r.choice(sep))
        s = ''.join(chars)
        return s.encode('ascii') + b"\x00"

    out += numericish(rng, 200)

    # 4) Binary blocks for memory operations (copy/swap). Keep small.
    def rand_bytes(n: int) -> bytes:
        return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

    # A few size-prefixed blobs can help parsers pick them up
    for size in (64, 128, 256):
        blob = rand_bytes(size)
        out += struct.pack("<I", size)
        out += blob

    # 5) More NUL-terminated UTF-16-ish data (bytes that will be cast to uint16 code units)
    utf16_units = bytearray()
    units = rng.randint(16, 128)
    for _ in range(units):
        utf16_units += struct.pack('<H', rng.randrange(0, 0x10000))
    utf16_units += b"\x00\x00"  # terminator unit
    out += utf16_units

    # 6) Ensure final size under limit
    return bytes(out[:4096])

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: ASCII string (NUL-terminated 7-bit ASCII, typically printable 0x20-0x7E)
# Fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR to initialize dng_string content and sometimes mask to printable ASCII.
# Provide an initial buffer that, when interpreted as a string by the harness, yields interesting yet valid
# ASCII-only content. We'll generate various lengths and patterns, including:
# - Empty string
# - Short words
# - Mixed cases, digits, punctuation
# - Long repeated patterns
# - Lines with different endings (but still within printable ASCII range)
# - Comma-separated numbers (to exercise NormalizeAsCommaSeparatedNumbers if used later)
# The harness likely treats the bytes as the backing data for FUZZ_PARAM_STR; we therefore avoid NUL within
# to not truncate unexpectedly and do not exceed 4096 bytes.

PRINTABLE = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(32, 127))  # space to ~ inclusive

words = [
    "",  # empty
    "A", "Z", "0", "9",
    "Hello", "World", "Adobe", "DNG", "SDK",
    "ascii", "PRINTABLE", "mixedCase", "Numbers123", "punctuation!?.",
]

punct = "!@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{};:',.<>/?|`~\""

def rand_printable(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(length))

def rand_word(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.randint(0, 6)
    if choice == 0:
        return rng.choice(words)
    elif choice == 1:
        # Alphanumeric
        alpha = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
        L = rng.randint(1, 24)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(alpha) for _ in range(L))
    elif choice == 2:
        # Punctuation-heavy
        L = rng.randint(1, 16)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(punct) for _ in range(L))
    elif choice == 3:
        # Repeated pattern
        base = rng.choice(["ab", "XY", "01", "!?"])
        reps = rng.randint(1, 32)
        return base * reps
    elif choice == 4:
        # Comma-separated numbers
        count = rng.randint(1, 20)
        nums = [str(rng.randint(0, 9999)) for _ in range(count)]
        return ','.join(nums)
    elif choice == 5:
        # Words with spaces
        count = rng.randint(1, 10)
        return ' '.join(rng.choice(words[1:]) for _ in range(count))
    else:
        # Arbitrary printable
        L = rng.randint(1, 64)
        return rand_printable(rng, L)

def compose_lines(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a multi-line ASCII string using \n or \r line endings (still printable when treated as chars here)
    line_sep = rng.choice(['\n', '\r'])
    line_count = rng.randint(1, 20)
    lines = [rand_word(rng) for _ in range(line_count)]
    return line_sep.join(lines)

def build_ascii_payload(rng: random.Random, target_size: int) -> str:
    # Mix different segments to reach target_size without exceeding it.
    segments: List[str] = []
    while True:
        # Randomly choose a segment type
        seg_type = rng.randint(0, 4)
        if seg_type == 0:
            seg = rand_word(rng)
        elif seg_type == 1:
            seg = compose_lines(rng)
        elif seg_type == 2:
            # Key=Value style pairs
            key = rand_word(rng).replace(' ', '')[:16] or 'K'
            val = rand_word(rng)[:32]
            seg = f"{key}={val}"
        elif seg_type == 3:
            # JSON-like ASCII (not strict JSON to keep fully printable)
            k = rand_word(rng).replace(' ', '')[:10] or 'k'
            v = rand_word(rng).replace('"', '')[:20]
            seg = f"{{\"{k}\":\"{v}\"}}"
        else:
            seg = rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(1, 40))
        # Ensure printable only and no NUL
        seg = ''.join(ch if ch in PRINTABLE else ' ' for ch in seg)
        if not segments:
            candidate = seg
        else:
            glue = rng.choice([' ', '\n', '\r', ''])
            candidate = glue.join([segments[-1], seg])
        if len(candidate) > target_size:
            break
        if segments:
            segments[-1] = candidate
        else:
            segments.append(candidate)
        if len(candidate) >= target_size // 2 and rng.random() < 0.3:
            break
    final = segments[-1] if segments else ''
    # Trim if slightly over (shouldn't be), and ensure not exceeding target
    return final[:target_size]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide overall size up to 1024 to leave headroom for harness
    size = rng.randint(0, 1024)
    # Occasionally generate very small or very large payloads within the cap
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.1:
        size = 0
    elif roll < 0.2:
        size = rng.randint(1, 16)
    elif roll > 0.95:
        size = rng.randint(1024, 2048)
    payload = build_ascii_payload(rng, size)
    # Ensure NUL-termination not required by harness buffer, but stubs call c_str(), which is handled by C++.
    # We only need to return raw bytes; avoid embedding NUL to keep full content.
    # Guarantee ASCII by filtering once more
    payload = ''.join(ch if ch in PRINTABLE else ' ' for ch in payload)
    # Limit to 4096 bytes
    data = payload.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')[:4096]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate interesting, valid byte buffers that represent NUL-terminated
# strings likely to be interpreted as either UTF-8 or system-encoded text.
# The fuzzer stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain arbitrary strings, which
# are then passed to Set_SystemEncoding or Set_UTF8_or_System.
# We therefore return a bytes buffer that contains a single string payload.
# The harness typically consumes the whole buffer as the source for FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# We include a terminating NUL to be safe for C-string APIs.

# Strategies included:
# - Pure ASCII printable strings
# - Strings with leading/trailing spaces and mixed case
# - Paths and filenames with separators
# - Locale-specific bytes that are valid in common 8-bit encodings (Latin-1, Windows-1252)
# - UTF-8 multibyte sequences (including emoji, CJK, accents)
# - Mixed content with NUL-termination
# - Edge cases: empty string, very long string (bounded), numbers, commas

ASCII_PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "

# Common Windows-1252 bytes that are non-ASCII but commonly seen in system encodings
WIN1252_BYTES = [
    0x80, # €
    0x82, # ‚
    0x83, # ƒ
    0x84, # „
    0x85, # …
    0x86, # †
    0x87, # ‡
    0x88, # ˆ
    0x89, # ‰
    0x8A, # Š
    0x8E, # Ž
    0x91, # ‘
    0x92, # ’
    0x93, # “
    0x94, # ”
    0x95, # •
    0x96, # –
    0x97, # —
    0x99, # ™
    0x9A, # š
    0x9E, # ž
    0xA0, # NBSP
    0xA1, 0xA2, 0xA3, 0xA9, 0xAE, 0xB0, 0xB1, 0xB5, 0xB7, 0xBC, 0xBD, 0xBE
]

# Some UTF-8 examples (as Python strings) to then encode to UTF-8 bytes
UTF8_EXAMPLES: List[str] = [
    "Café crème",
    "naïve façade coöperate",
    "こんにちは世界",           # Japanese
    "Привет мир",             # Russian
    "مرحبا بالعالم",          # Arabic
    "γειά σου Κόσμε",        # Greek
    "你好，世界",              # Chinese
    "안녕하세요 세계",         # Korean
    "emoji: 😀😇🏳️\u200d🌈",
    "Straße – München — Köln ™",
]

# Some system-like path strings
PATH_EXAMPLES = [
    r"C:\\Program Files\\Adobe\\DNG\\bin",
    r"C:\\Users\\User Name\\Documents\\测试\\фото",
    r"/usr/local/share/dng/примеры",
    r"./relative/path/naïve-file.txt",
]

# Some CSV/numeric strings to trigger numeric parsing paths in utilities
CSV_EXAMPLES = [
    "1,2,3,4,5",
    "0, -1, 42, 3.14159, -273.15",
]

# JIS-like ASCII with escapes (still ASCII-safe)
ASCII_EXAMPLES = [
    "Hello World",
    "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
    "   leading and trailing spaces   \r\n",
    "Mixed-CASE_value_Name",
    "key=value; path=/; HttpOnly",
]

# Build a bytes payload from chosen strategy

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len=0, max_len=64) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))
    return s.encode('ascii')


def _rand_win1252(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=64) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            out.append(rng.choice(list(range(0x20, 0x7F))))  # ASCII printable
        else:
            out.append(rng.choice(WIN1252_BYTES))
    return bytes(out)


def _rand_utf8(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix from predefined and random composition
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        s = rng.choice(UTF8_EXAMPLES)
    else:
        # Compose random mixed string
        parts: List[str] = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
            choice = rng.random()
            if choice < 0.4:
                parts.append(''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + ' ') for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10))))
            elif choice < 0.7:
                parts.append(rng.choice(UTF8_EXAMPLES))
            else:
                parts.append(''.join(chr(rng.randint(0x00C0, 0x024F)) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6))))  # Latin ext
        s = ' '.join(parts)
    return s.encode('utf-8')


def _choose_base_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choices = []
    choices.extend([bytes()] * 1)  # empty string case
    choices.extend([ex.encode('utf-8') for ex in ASCII_EXAMPLES])
    choices.extend([ex.encode('utf-8') for ex in PATH_EXAMPLES])
    choices.extend([ex.encode('utf-8') for ex in CSV_EXAMPLES])
    choices.extend([ex.encode('utf-8') for ex in UTF8_EXAMPLES])
    strategies = [
        lambda: rng.choice(choices),
        lambda: _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 128),
        lambda: _rand_utf8(rng),
        lambda: _rand_win1252(rng, 1, 128),
    ]
    # Bias towards valid UTF-8/system strings
    strat = rng.choices(strategies, weights=[2, 3, 4, 3], k=1)[0]
    return strat()


def _maybe_terminate(rng: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure NUL-termination for C-string APIs
    if not data or data[-1] != 0:
        data += b"\x00"
    return data


def _maybe_repeat(rng: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Occasionally repeat the string with separators to exercise longer inputs
    if len(data) < 512 and rng.random() < 0.25:
        sep = rng.choice([b"\n", b"\r\n", b";", b", "])
        times = rng.randint(2, 6)
        core = data.rstrip(b"\x00")
        joined = sep.join([core] * times)
        return _maybe_terminate(rng, joined)
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    payload = _choose_base_payload(rng)
    payload = _maybe_repeat(rng, payload)
    payload = payload[:4095]  # leave room for terminator
    payload = _maybe_terminate(rng, payload)
    return payload

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for JIS X 0208:1990 encoded NUL-terminated byte strings.
# dng_string::Set_JIS_X208_1990 expects a C-string in that encoding and will
# convert to internal UTF-8. We provide plausible Shift_JIS byte sequences
# (common exterior encoding for JIS X 0208). We avoid invalid lead/trail bytes
# and include mixtures of ASCII, Kana, Kanji, punctuation, and NUL termination.

ASCII_BYTES = list(range(0x20, 0x7F))  # printable ASCII
ASCII_SPACES = [0x09, 0x20]  # TAB and space

# Katakana half-width (common in Shift_JIS, but strictly JIS X 0201). Some decoders accept it.
HALF_KATA = list(range(0xA6, 0xDF))

# Two-byte lead byte ranges for Shift_JIS (mapped to JIS X 0208):
LEAD_RANGES = [
    (0x81, 0x9F),
    (0xE0, 0xEF),
]
# Valid trail byte ranges (excluding 0x7F):
TRAIL_RANGES = [
    (0x40, 0x7E),
    (0x80, 0xFC),
]

# Some useful punctuation or symbols in JIS X 0208 that in Shift_JIS are two-byte
# sequences; we include a small curated set of known-good pairs for added validity.
KNOWN_SJIS_PAIRS = [
    b"\x81\x40",  # IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE
    b"\x81\x5B",  # MIDDLE DOT
    b"\x81\x5C",  # KATAKANA MIDDLE DOT (similar)
    b"\x81\x69",  # FULLWIDTH OPENING PAREN
    b"\x81\x6A",  # FULLWIDTH CLOSING PAREN
    b"\x82\xA0",  # HIRAGANA LETTER A
    b"\x83\x40",  # KATAKANA LETTER A
    b"\x82\x9F",  # HIRAGANA SMALL TU
    b"\x83\x93",  # KATAKANA LETTER N
]

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[int]) -> int:
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]

def _rand_in_ranges(rng: random.Random, ranges: List[tuple]) -> int:
    r = rng.choice(ranges)
    return rng.randint(r[0], r[1])

def _emit_ascii(rng: random.Random, out: bytearray, length: int):
    for _ in range(length):
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            out.append(_rand_choice(rng, ASCII_SPACES))
        else:
            out.append(_rand_choice(rng, ASCII_BYTES))

def _emit_half_katakana(rng: random.Random, out: bytearray, length: int):
    for _ in range(length):
        out.append(_rand_choice(rng, HALF_KATA))

def _emit_two_byte_sjis(rng: random.Random, out: bytearray, pairs: int):
    for _ in range(pairs):
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            # Use a known-good pair sometimes
            out.extend(rng.choice(KNOWN_SJIS_PAIRS))
        else:
            lead = _rand_in_ranges(rng, LEAD_RANGES)
            # ensure trail != 0x7F
            while True:
                trail = _rand_in_ranges(rng, TRAIL_RANGES)
                if trail != 0x7F:
                    break
            out.append(lead)
            out.append(trail)

def _emit_mixed_segment(rng: random.Random, out: bytearray, target_len: int):
    # Mix ASCII, half-width katakana, and two-byte SJIS sequences.
    while len(out) < target_len:
        choice = rng.random()
        remain = target_len - len(out)
        if choice < 0.4 and remain >= 1:
            _emit_ascii(rng, out, rng.randint(1, min(8, remain)))
        elif choice < 0.6 and remain >= 1:
            _emit_half_katakana(rng, out, rng.randint(1, min(6, remain)))
        else:
            pairs = max(1, rng.randint(1, min(4, remain // 2 if remain >= 2 else 1)))
            _emit_two_byte_sjis(rng, out, pairs)
            if len(out) > target_len:
                # trim if exceeded
                del out[target_len:]
                break

def _add_esc_sequences(rng: random.Random, out: bytearray):
    # Some implementations accept ISO-2022-JP escape sequences to switch to JIS 0208.
    # We optionally add a small well-formed sequence around a short block.
    if rng.random() < 0.25 and len(out) < 4000:
        # ESC $ B ... ESC ( B
        start = b"\x1B$B"
        end = b"\x1B(B"
        # Insert at a random position
        pos = rng.randint(0, len(out))
        block = bytearray()
        _emit_two_byte_sjis(rng, block, rng.randint(2, 6))
        out[pos:pos] = start + block + end

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide overall length (excluding final NUL); keep <= 4095
    total_len = rng.randint(16, 512) if rng.random() < 0.7 else rng.randint(513, 2048)

    segments = rng.randint(2, 6)
    # Allocate lengths for segments
    base = total_len // segments
    remainder = total_len % segments

    out = bytearray()

    for i in range(segments):
        seg_len = base + (1 if i < remainder else 0)
        # Ensure at least room for 1 byte
        seg_len = max(1, seg_len)
        # Start segments with plausible context markers
        if i == 0 and rng.random() < 0.5:
            # Add an ASCII header-like prefix sometimes
            prefix = rng.choice([
                b"ISO-2022-JP:", b"Shift_JIS:", b"JIS0208:", b"\xef\xbb\xbf", b"# "])
            out.extend(prefix)
        _emit_mixed_segment(rng, out, len(out) + seg_len)
        # Add small known pairs between segments
        if i < segments - 1 and rng.random() < 0.6:
            out.extend(rng.choice(KNOWN_SJIS_PAIRS))

    # Optionally add escape sequences to simulate ISO-2022-JP switching to JIS 0208
    _add_esc_sequences(rng, out)

    # Ensure we end on character boundary: avoid dangling lead byte
    if out and (0x81 <= out[-1] <= 0x9F or 0xE0 <= out[-1] <= 0xEF):
        # Complete with a valid trail
        trail = _rand_in_ranges(rng, TRAIL_RANGES)
        if trail == 0x7F:
            trail = 0x7E
        out.append(trail)

    # Trim to max allowed minus NUL
    if len(out) > 4095:
        out = out[:4095]

    # Ensure not empty after trimming
    if not out:
        out.append(0x41)  # 'A'

    # NUL-terminate for C-string expectation
    out.append(0)

    return bytes(out)

import random
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

# Generate a valid EXIF date-time string: "YYYY:MM:DD HH:MM:SS"
# Return as bytes to seed the fuzzers' FUZZ_PARAM_STR and filename sources.

def _random_valid_datetime(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a reasonable year range that typical EXIF supports
    year = rng.randint(1900, 2100)
    # Generate a random day offset from a base date to always be valid
    start = datetime(year, 1, 1)
    end = datetime(year, 12, 31)
    delta_days = (end - start).days
    day = rng.randint(0, delta_days)
    d = start + timedelta(days=day,
                          hours=rng.randint(0, 23),
                          minutes=rng.randint(0, 59),
                          seconds=rng.randint(0, 59))
    return d.strftime("%Y:%m:%d %H:%M:%S")


def _random_edge_datetime(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct edge cases that are still valid per EXIF and may hit boundaries
    candidates = []
    # Leap day valid case
    candidates.append("2000:02:29 00:00:00")  # Leap year
    # End of month boundaries
    candidates.extend([
        "1999:01:31 23:59:59",
        "2001:02:28 23:59:59",
        "2004:02:29 23:59:59",  # leap year
        "2012:12:31 00:00:00",
    ])
    # Minimal and maximal plausible years in EXIF contexts
    candidates.extend([
        "1900:01:01 00:00:00",
        "2100:12:31 23:59:59",
    ])
    return rng.choice(candidates)


def _random_near_boundary_valid(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate dates with components near limits but still valid
    year = rng.choice([1900, 1970, 1999, 2000, 2099, 2100])
    # Pick a month then choose a valid day for that month accounting for leap years
    month = rng.randint(1, 12)
    # Compute last day of month
    # For February, consider leap year rule similar to Gregorian
    if month in (1,3,5,7,8,10,12):
        last_day = 31
    elif month in (4,6,9,11):
        last_day = 30
    else:
        # February
        leap = (year % 400 == 0) or (year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0)
        last_day = 29 if leap else 28
    # Day either 1 or last day
    day = rng.choice([1, last_day])
    hour = rng.choice([0, 23])
    minute = rng.choice([0, 59])
    second = rng.choice([0, 59])
    return f"{year:04d}:{month:02d}:{day:02d} {hour:02d}:{minute:02d}:{second:02d}"


def _random_valid_or_noise(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mostly return valid EXIF strings to exercise success paths, sometimes return harmless variants
    p = rng.random()
    if p < 0.7:
        return _random_valid_datetime(rng)
    elif p < 0.9:
        return _random_near_boundary_valid(rng)
    else:
        return _random_edge_datetime(rng)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Build a small corpus of plausible inputs separated by newlines, with the first line
    # being the primary candidate (what FUZZ_PARAM_STR is likely to use).
    # Keeping under 4096 bytes total.
    primary = _random_valid_or_noise(rng)

    # Add a few additional valid timestamps to enrich the input buffer for consumers
    extras = [
        _random_valid_datetime(rng),
        _random_near_boundary_valid(rng),
        _random_edge_datetime(rng),
    ]

    # Combine lines. Some fuzz harnesses may read the first line or a slice.
    lines = [primary] + extras
    payload = ("\n".join(lines)).encode("ascii")
    return payload[:4096]

import random
import datetime

def _rand_choice_weighted(rng, items):
    # items: list of (weight, value)
    total = sum(w for w, _ in items)
    x = rng.uniform(0, total)
    acc = 0.0
    for w, v in items:
        acc += w
        if x <= acc:
            return v
    return items[-1][1]

def _fmt_tz_offset(rng):
    # Generate timezone: 'Z' or "+HH:MM" or "-HH:MM"
    choice = _rand_choice_weighted(rng, [
        (0.5, 'Z'),
        (0.3, '+'),
        (0.2, '-')
    ])
    if choice == 'Z':
        return 'Z'
    # Offsets from -12:00 to +14:00 are common; ISO allows up to ±15:00
    max_h = 15
    h = rng.randint(0, max_h)
    m = rng.choice([0, 15, 30, 45])
    return f"{choice}{h:02d}:{m:02d}"

def _maybe_fractional_seconds(rng):
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        digits = rng.randint(1, 9)
        frac = ''.join(str(rng.randint(0, 9)) for _ in range(digits))
        return f".{frac}"
    return ''

def _basic_or_extended(rng, dt):
    # Extended: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss, Basic: YYYYMMDDThhmmss
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'), True
    else:
        return dt.strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S'), False

def _week_date(rng, dt):
    # ISO week date: YYYY-Www-D
    iso_year, iso_week, iso_weekday = dt.isocalendar()
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return f"{iso_year}-W{iso_week:02d}-{iso_weekday}"
    else:
        return f"{iso_year}W{iso_week:02d}{iso_weekday}"

def _ordinal_date(rng, dt):
    # Ordinal date: YYYY-DDD
    day_of_year = int(dt.strftime('%j'))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return f"{dt.year}-{day_of_year:03d}"
    else:
        return f"{dt.year}{day_of_year:03d}"

def _time_only(rng, dt):
    # Time only: hh:mm:ss or hhmmss with optional fraction and TZ
    t = dt.strftime('%H:%M:%S') if rng.random() < 0.7 else dt.strftime('%H%M%S')
    t += _maybe_fractional_seconds(rng)
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        t += _fmt_tz_offset(rng)
    return t

def _date_only(rng, dt):
    # Date only variants
    pick = rng.random()
    if pick < 0.5:
        return dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
    elif pick < 0.8:
        return _ordinal_date(rng, dt)
    else:
        return _week_date(rng, dt)

def _datetime_with_sep(rng, dt):
    # Build date + time with T or space sep, optional fraction and TZ
    base, extended = _basic_or_extended(rng, dt)
    # If basic, no colons in time; but we already formatted accordingly
    frac = _maybe_fractional_seconds(rng)
    tz = _fmt_tz_offset(rng)
    sep = 'T' if rng.random() < 0.85 else ' '
    # If base already includes 'T', keep as is; otherwise construct from parts
    if 'T' in base:
        s = base + frac + tz
    else:
        # base is like YYYYMMDDThhmmss (contains T). If sep override requested space, replace
        if sep != 'T':
            base = base.replace('T', sep)
        s = base + frac + tz
    return s

def _random_plausible_datetime(rng):
    # Dates within wide valid range 0001..9999 (Python supports 1..9999)
    year = rng.randint(1, 9999)
    # For variety, sometimes choose leap day capable months
    month = rng.randint(1, 12)
    # Determine max day for month/year
    if month in (1,3,5,7,8,10,12):
        mdays = 31
    elif month in (4,6,9,11):
        mdays = 30
    else:
        # February
        leap = (year % 4 == 0 and (year % 100 != 0 or year % 400 == 0))
        mdays = 29 if leap else 28
    day = rng.randint(1, mdays)
    hour = rng.randint(0, 23)
    minute = rng.randint(0, 59)
    second = rng.randint(0, 59)
    micro = rng.randint(0, 999999)
    return datetime.datetime(year, month, day, hour, minute, second, micro)

def _make_iso8601_strings(rng, count):
    out = []
    for _ in range(count):
        dt = _random_plausible_datetime(rng)
        form = rng.random()
        if form < 0.55:
            s = _datetime_with_sep(rng, dt)
        elif form < 0.75:
            # Date only
            s = _date_only(rng, dt)
        elif form < 0.9:
            # Time only
            s = _time_only(rng, dt)
        else:
            # Week date with time
            date_part = _week_date(rng, dt)
            time_part = dt.strftime('%H:%M:%S') + _maybe_fractional_seconds(rng)
            sep = 'T' if rng.random() < 0.9 else ' '
            s = f"{date_part}{sep}{time_part}{_fmt_tz_offset(rng)}"
        out.append(s)
    return out

def _edge_cases():
    # A set of interesting boundary and special values
    return [
        '0001-01-01T00:00:00Z',
        '9999-12-31T23:59:59+14:00',
        '1970-01-01T00:00:00Z',
        '2000-02-29T12:34:56Z',
        '2001-02-28T23:59:59-12:00',
        '2020-12-31T23:59:59.999999Z',
        '2020-366',                 # ordinal date leap year
        '2021-365',                 # ordinal date non-leap
        '2021-W01-1',               # ISO week date
        '2021W011',                 # basic week date
        'T00:00:00Z',               # time-only with leading T (allowed by some parsers)
        '24:00:00Z',                # midnight at end of day representation
        '2023-03-10 15:26:40+00:00',# space separator
        '20230310T152640Z',         # basic datetime Z
        '2023-03-10T15:26:40+00:30',
        '2023-03-10T15:26:40-05:00',
        '2023-03-10T15:26:40.123',
        '2023-03-10',               # date only
        '15:26:40Z',                # time only
    ]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Build a corpus of ISO 8601 strings combining edge cases and randomized valid ones
    strings = []
    # Always include several edge cases
    edge = _edge_cases()
    rng.shuffle(edge)
    strings.extend(edge[:rng.randint(6, len(edge))])
    # Add a set of randomized plausible datetimes
    strings.extend(_make_iso8601_strings(rng, rng.randint(8, 20)))
    # Occasionally duplicate one string many times to explore caching/branching
    if rng.random() < 0.2 and strings:
        dup = rng.choice(strings)
        strings.extend([dup] * rng.randint(3, 7))
    # Join with NUL separators to provide multiple candidates; fuzzer may slice
    payload = ('\x00'.join(strings)).encode('utf-8')
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(payload) > 4096:
        payload = payload[:4096]
    return payload

import random
from datetime import date, timedelta

# Target format: IPTC date string YYYYMMDD (8 digits, no separators)
# The fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() if its size % 5 == 0.
# Generate valid dates, include edge cases, and ensure length multiple of 5.

EDGE_DATES = [
    (1, 1, 1),
    (1582, 10, 15),
    (1900, 2, 28),
    (1900, 3, 1),
    (1999, 12, 31),
    (2000, 2, 29),
    (2000, 1, 1),
    (2001, 1, 1),
    (2020, 2, 29),
    (2099, 12, 31),
    (2999, 12, 31),
]

def _valid_iptc(y: int, m: int, d: int) -> str:
    # Adjust to a valid calendar date if needed by clamping day then month
    m = min(max(m, 1), 12)
    # Try to decrement day until valid
    while d >= 1:
        try:
            date(y, m, d)
            return f"{y:04d}{m:02d}{d:02d}"
        except ValueError:
            d -= 1
    # Fallback to first of the month
    return f"{y:04d}{m:02d}01"

def _random_valid_date(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Pick a random offset within range and construct a valid date directly
    start = date(1, 1, 1)
    total_days = (date(2999, 12, 31) - start).days
    offset = rng.randint(0, total_days)
    dt = start + timedelta(days=offset)
    # Occasionally bias the year toward extremes by remapping via a safe method
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        y = rng.randint(1, 2999)
        # Remap by keeping month/day where possible, adjust day if invalid
        s = _valid_iptc(y, dt.month, dt.day)
        return s
    return f"{dt.year:04d}{dt.month:02d}{dt.day:02d}"

def _pad_to_len_multiple_of_5(s: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    rem = len(s) % 5
    need = (5 - rem) % 5
    if need == 0:
        return s
    extra = []
    while len("".join(extra)) < need:
        extra.append(_random_valid_date(rng))
    return s + ("".join(extra))[:need]

def _edge_or_random(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            y, m, d = rng.choice(EDGE_DATES)
            s = _valid_iptc(y, m, d)
        else:
            s = _random_valid_date(rng)
    else:
        parts = [_random_valid_date(rng)]
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            parts.append(_random_valid_date(rng))
        s = "".join(parts)
    s = _pad_to_len_multiple_of_5(s, rng)
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    s = _edge_or_random(rng)
    if len(s) > 4096:
        s = s[: 4096 - (len(s) % 5 or 5)]
        if not s:
            s = _pad_to_len_multiple_of_5(_random_valid_date(rng), rng)
    return s.encode('ascii')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: IPTC time string
# Format: HHMMSS optionally followed by a timezone offset "+/-HHMM"
# - HH: 00-23
# - MM: 00-59
# - SS: 00-59
# - TZ: sign + two-digit hours 00-23 (or up to 24?) and two-digit minutes 00-59. IPTC commonly allows +/-HHMM up to +/-2359.
# The fuzzer stub sometimes uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() as the candidate string if its length % 7 == 0; otherwise it uses a synthesized valid string.
# Therefore, to influence the path that uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR, we should often provide a buffer length that is a multiple of 7 and contain a valid IPTC time (with or without timezone).
# We will generate multiple concatenated candidate strings (separated by NUL or newline) so that the harness can slice as needed.

# Strategy:
# - Build one or more IPTC time strings:
#   * Pure time: HHMMSS (6 chars)
#   * Time + timezone: HHMMSS+HHMM or HHMMSS-HHMM (11 chars)
# - Additionally craft edge/timezone boundary cases and invalid-but-well-formed variants (still numeric) to exercise parsing paths while staying mostly valid.
# - Ensure total buffer length is <= 4096 and often multiple of 7 to trigger FUZZ_PARAM_STR usage in the stub.
# - Return as bytes.


def _rnd(rng: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(a, b)


def _fmt2(n: int) -> str:
    return f"{n:02d}"


def make_time(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    hh = _rnd(rng, 0, 23)
    mm = _rnd(rng, 0, 59)
    ss = _rnd(rng, 0, 59)
    return _fmt2(hh) + _fmt2(mm) + _fmt2(ss)


def make_tz(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # IPTC offset typically up to +/-2359. Also allow 0000 edge.
    sign = rng.choice(['+', '-'])
    # Bias towards valid minute ranges 00, 15, 30, 45 and edge 59
    tz_h = _rnd(rng, 0, 23)
    tz_m = rng.choice([0, 15, 30, 45, 59]) if rng.random() < 0.8 else _rnd(rng, 0, 59)
    return f"{sign}{_fmt2(tz_h)}{_fmt2(tz_m)}"


def make_valid_iptc_time(rng: random.Random, with_tz: bool) -> str:
    base = make_time(rng)
    return base + (make_tz(rng) if with_tz else "")


def make_edge_cases(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cases = []
    # Exact boundaries
    cases.append("000000")
    cases.append("235959")
    # With timezone extremes and zeros
    for sign in ['+', '-']:
        cases.append("000000" + f"{sign}0000")
        cases.append("235959" + f"{sign}2359")
        cases.append("120000" + f"{sign}1245")
    # Minute boundaries
    for m in ["000000", "005900", "015959", "095959"]:
        cases.append(m)
    # Common real-world like times
    cases.extend([
        "081530+0000",
        "123000-0500",
        "172245+0530",
        "210101+0900",
    ])
    return cases


def pad_to_multiple_of_7(s: str) -> str:
    # Make overall length multiple of 7 by appending spaces (ignored by parser if trimmed) or newline.
    # Safer: append a single newline which some parsers ignore; but unknown here. We'll append '0' which keeps numeric.
    rem = (-len(s)) % 7
    if rem:
        s += '0' * rem
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    items: List[str] = []

    # Add several valid items, mix with and without TZ
    count = 5 + _rnd(rng, 0, 10)
    for _ in range(count):
        with_tz = rng.random() < 0.7
        items.append(make_valid_iptc_time(rng, with_tz))

    # Edge cases
    items.extend(make_edge_cases(rng))

    # Create some strings whose lengths are exactly multiples of 7 to trigger FUZZ_PARAM_STR path
    # If not multiple, pad the concatenated buffer later.
    # Also include repeats to create longer buffers.
    rng.shuffle(items)

    # Occasionally include sequences concatenated without separators (parser likely reads C-string until NUL; fuzzer may slice)
    # We'll join with newlines to separate logically, but overall buffer length will be adjusted to multiple of 7.
    joined = "\n".join(items)

    # Also add a focused candidate at start: ensure one prime candidate of length multiple of 7
    primary = make_valid_iptc_time(rng, with_tz=True)
    primary = pad_to_multiple_of_7(primary)

    payload = primary + "\n" + joined

    # Ensure total length <= 4096; if too long, truncate at a boundary (end of line) and then pad to multiple of 7
    if len(payload) > 4096:
        # Truncate to last newline within limit for clean cut
        cut = payload.rfind("\n", 0, 4096)
        if cut <= 0:
            payload = payload[:4096]
        else:
            payload = payload[:cut]

    # Finally pad whole buffer to multiple of 7 to increase chance harness treats FUZZ_PARAM_STR candidate
    payload = pad_to_multiple_of_7(payload)

    # Encode as ASCII bytes
    return payload.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
